In SLR [5], lack of real-time metrics (e.g., cyclomatic complexity, dynamic function calls, no of unused objects and variables) to monitor and control the actual software development progress is observed to be least discussed. A survey in Finish software industry specifically reported lack of realtime metrics used during software development process. In this survey, we realized that 89% of organizations don't use real-time metrics as shown in Figure 18. (An Evaluation of Software Measurement Processes in Pakistani Software Industry, page 1)

Object-oriented metrics are used to predict the quality of object-oriented software. The attributes that determine software quality include maintainability, fault tolerance, understandability, fault density, standardized rework rate, reusability, etc. Several studies were carried out, including the empirical verification of the object-oriented metrics in open source software for the prediction of faults using CBO, LOC, LCOM, NOC and DIT [10], reuse analysis of objectoriented systems using metrics of inheritance, coupling and cohesion [92], heuristic review of CK metrics [93], reusable metrics for object-oriented design [94] and empirical analysis of CK metrics for object-oriented design complexity [95]. (Experimental Validation of Inheritance Metrics’ Impact on Software Fault Prediction, page 5)

TABLE 5. Mitigation strategies for key issues found in the survey. Pada penelitian ini, ditemukan bahwa sebagian besar perusahaan di industri software Pakistan tidak menggunakan metrik waktu nyata untuk mengukur dan mengontrol proses pengembangan perangkat lunak mereka. Hanya 11% saja dari perusahaan yang menggunakan metrik waktu nyata seperti cyclomatic complexity, dynamic function calls, jumlah obyek dan variabel yang tidak digunakan. Kebanyakan perusahaan juga tidak memiliki kamus ukuran yang komprehensif. Dari total 57 responden, hanya 38% saja yang memiliki kamus ukuran lengkap, sementara 19% menggunakan kamus ukuran secara parsial dan 16% tidak menggunakan kamus ukuran sama sekali. Dalam hal penggunaan data historis untuk prediksi, kurang dari 50% perusahaan yang diwawancarai mengaku sering menggunakan data historis tersebut. Bahkan sekitar 58% perusahaan di industri software Pakistan tidak memiliki kriteria validasi metrik sama sekali. Selain itu, penelitian ini juga menemukan bahwa model keberhasilan implementasi proses pengukuran berbasis MP dapat dibangun dengan analisis SLR. Dalam model tersebut, ada tiga faktor utama yang mempengaruhi sukses atau tidaknya implementasi proses pengukuran: faktor eksternal, adaptasi ukuran, dan penerimaan ukuran. Model ini kemudian diperkuat dengan hasil analisis statistik multivariat terhadap respons 200 profesional perangkat lunak. Hasil analisis menunjukkan bahwa model keberhasilan implementasi proses pengukuran berbasis MP memiliki faktor-faktor yang signifikan dan dapat membantu meningkatkan efisiensi proses pengembangan perangkat lunak. (An Evaluation of Software Measurement Processes in Pakistani Software Industry, page 16)

Bagaimana machine learning diterapkan dalam software development?

[26] introduced DL to software language modeling based on information retrieval models. Design pattern prediction primarily focuses on recognizing design patterns in software through source code or user interface layout using ML techniques. For example, Nguyen et al. [27] proposed an approach known as DeepUI in order to semi-automate the design tasks by learning from previous UI design patterns. Development effort estimation refers to estimating effort for the development of software projects using ML techniques. Ionescu [28] used ANN to automate effort estimation by learning from textual features of project tasks. (A Literature Review of Using Machine Learning in Software Development Life Cycle Stages, page 6)

2. The software engineering (SE) community is continuously looking for better and more efficient ways of building high-quality software systems. However, in practice, the strong emphasis on time to market tends to ignore many, well-known SE recommendations. That is, practitioners focus more on programming as compared to requirements gathering, planning, specification, architecture, design, and documentation -all of which are ultimately known to greatly benefit the cost-effectiveness and quality of software systems. Lack of human resources is often cited as the main reason for doing so. Herein lies the great potential for machine learning (ML) since its algorithms are proven to be most befitting to problem domains that aim to replicate human behavior. Moreover, the key advantages and disadvantages of using ML for software testing are discussed. Mainly, the advantage of ML techniques is their scalability and efficient application to large-scale and complex software systems. The disadvantage, on the other hand, is the unavailability of data that fits well with the learning process. (A Literature Review of Using Machine Learning in Software Development Life Cycle Stages, page 1)

### user_input

Apa itu software maintenance?

### retrieved_context

1. The maintenance phase follows the entire life cycle of the software. If users or developers find a problem, it may be fixed or corrected ahead of the next release, depending on how serious it is. (Systematic Mapping: Artificial Intelligence Techniques in Software Engineering, page 4)

2. Autonomous agents are now tackling software maintenance jobs that used to demand a lot of human time and expertise. The most ambitious of these are bug-fixing agents. They comb through error logs, look for patterns in failures, pinpoint the offending lines of code and generate their own fixes so the software keeps running smoothly [22], [38], [39]. Other agents focus on improving code quality. They detect ''code smells,'' suggest better designs and carry out refactoring work that would otherwise be slow and error-prone for human developers [40]. There are also migration agents that help organisations modernise legacy software by adapting it to new platforms, updated libraries or newer language versions [2]. Recent studies show that large language models can even serve as lightweight testers, reproducing bugs with very little input to aid automated debugging [33]. Taken together, these maintenance agents help keep software up to date while cutting down on the technical debt that can build up in large systems. (Methods and Techniques of Agentic Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review, page 13)

3. The software maintenance stage has been found as the least focused stage for researchers in this domain. In this category, the research is more inclined towards cost/effort estimation than the rest of the maintenance tasks. We found articles focusing on software maintainability prediction, which refers to the proposed ML techniques in order to assist the prediction of maintainability metrics appropriate for specific software projects [45]. Software aging detection refers to the use of ML in order to detect software maturity and its aging in terms of resource depletion such as memory leaks, high CPU usage, and overtime. In this regard, Andrzejak et al. [46] investigated the feasibility of ML techniques for classification in detecting early performance degradation due to software image aging. The maintenance effort estimation class aims at estimating the amount of effort required for the maintenance of a software system using ML, e.g., Chandra et al. [47] used an SVM-based regression model in order to forecast maintenance effort with univariate and multivariate approaches. In the software industry, it is common to classify projects that satisfy the triple constraint as successful [2]. (Team Formation in Software Engineering: A Systematic Mapping Study, page 1)

Analisis terbaru mengenai komponen kualitas perangkat lunak (software quality) dalam menengahi dampak modal intelektual (intellectual capital) pada kesuksesan perusahaan swasta open-source software (COSS) telah membawa beberapa temuan penting. Data yang dianalisis menunjukkan bahwa ada hubungan positif signifikan antara kualitas perangkat lunak dan kesuksesan COSS (β = 0,581, T-value = 10,842, P-value = 0,000). Sebenarnya, kualitas perangkat lunak memainkan peran mediasi yang signifikan dalam menengahi hubungan antara modal intelektual dan kesuksesan COSS.

Penelitian ini juga menemukan bahwa ada hubungan positif antara kapital struktural (structural capital) dan kualitas perangkat lunak, serta antara kapital manusia (human capital) dan kualitas perangkat lunak. Dalam beberapa kasus, mediasi efektif kapital manusia pada relasi tersebut terbukti signifikan.

Kemudian, hasil analisis menunjukkan bahwa kualitas perangkat lunak merupakan faktor yang sangat penting dalam mempengaruhi kesuksesan COSS. Dengan demikian, penelitian ini mendukung asumsi-asumsi yang telah diusulkan (H1-H11) mengenai hubungan antara modal intelektual dan kualitas perangkat lunak terhadap kesuksesan COSS.

Dari hasil analisis, dapat disimpulkan bahwa kualitas perangkat lunak merupakan faktor penting dalam menengahi dampak kapital manusia terhadap kesuksesan COSS. Hasil ini dapat dijadikan sebagai rujukan bagi pihak manajemen dan strategis dalam mengembangkan kebijakan yang lebih efektif untuk meningkatkan kinerja perusahaan open-source software mereka. 7. In order to effectively coordinate and evaluate software quality management efforts, software companies use software quality models [34], [37], [44], [45]. The earliest software quality model was proposed by McCall in 1976. The McCall model was later revised by Boehm and Dromey [41], [44], [46], [47]. Recently developed software quality evaluation models include ISO/IEC 25010 which outlines 8 attributes to be used for software quality assessment. In contrast, the earlier version ISO/IEC 9126 adopts 6 characteristics [44], [45], [48].

Despite being viewed as a useful tool for quality assurance [44], software standards or models lack functionality and practical application owing to the ambiguity involved [37], [47]. Gorla and Lin as cited in [49] propose a software quality assessment model that includes relevance and usefulness (i.e., functionality), usability, maintainability, and reliability attributes. On the other hand, other scholars identify usability, reliability, functionality, performance efficiency, portability, and maintainability as important quality measurements [40], [46]. Similarly, several studies identify functionality, usability, reliability, performance efficiency, and maintainability as the most impactful measures of software quality [14], [41], [43], [45]. The software maintenance stage has been found as the least focused stage for researchers in this domain. In this category, the research is more inclined towards cost/effort estimation than the rest of the maintenance tasks. We found articles focusing on software maintainability prediction, which refers to the proposed ML techniques in order to assist the prediction of maintainability metrics appropriate for specific software projects [45]. Software aging detection refers to the use of ML in order to detect software maturity and its aging in terms of resource depletion such as memory leaks, high CPU usage, and overtime. In this regard, Andrzejak et al. [46] investigated the feasibility of ML techniques for classification in detecting early performance degradation due to software image aging. The maintenance effort estimation class aims at estimating the amount of effort required for the maintenance of a software system using ML, e.g., Chandra et al. [47] used an SVM-based regression model in order to forecast maintenance effort with univariate and multivariate approaches. (A Literature Review of Using Machine Learning in Software Development Life Cycle Stages, page 7)

Autonomous agents are now tackling software maintenance jobs that used to demand a lot of human time and expertise. The most ambitious of these are bug-fixing agents. They comb through error logs, look for patterns in failures, pinpoint the offending lines of code and generate their own fixes so the software keeps running smoothly [22], [38], [39]. Other agents focus on improving code quality. They detect ''code smells,'' suggest better designs and carry out refactoring work that would otherwise be slow and error-prone for human developers [40]. There are also migration agents that help organisations modernise legacy software by adapting it to new platforms, updated libraries or newer language versions [2]. Recent studies show that large language models can even serve as lightweight testers, reproducing bugs with very little input to aid automated debugging [33]. Taken together, these maintenance agents help keep software up to date while cutting down on the technical debt that can build up in large systems. (Methods and Techniques of Agentic Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review, page 13)

The maintenance phase follows the entire life cycle of the software. If users or developers find a problem, it may be fixed or corrected ahead of the next release, depending on how serious it is. (Systematic Mapping: Artificial Intelligence Techniques in Software Engineering, page 4)

Typically machine learning focus on design and development of algorithms with techniques. That extricate rules, and patterns from massive databases. Neural Networks (NN) are previously being utilized within the software to create reliability growth models for the prediction of total modification or reusability metrics. The NN model is trained to do again a stipulated series of exact instances classification, as an alternative to creating formulas or rules. Mahajan et. al [38] mentioned that machine learning methods are beneficial to determine software faults as complete processing is performed by the computer. (Efficacy of Inheritance Aspect in Software Fault Prediction—A Survey Paper, page 1)

The software engineering (SE) community is continuously looking for better and more efficient ways of building high-quality software systems. However, in practice, the strong emphasis on time to market tends to ignore many, well-known SE recommendations. That is, practitioners focus more on programming as compared to requirements gathering, planning, specification, architecture, design, and documentation -all of which are ultimately known to greatly benefit the cost-effectiveness and quality of software systems. Lack of human resources is often cited as the main reason for doing so. Herein lies the great potential for machine learning (ML) since its algorithms are proven to be most befitting to problem domains that aim to replicate human behavior. Hence, it stands to reason that human-centric SE activities should also benefit from ML [1]. (A Literature Review of Using Machine Learning in Software Development Life Cycle Stages, page 1)

The prediction of defects in software systems is a highly active research area. For instance, Hall et al. [7] have identified, in a systematic review of SDP, 208 studies on defect prediction, all published between 2000 and 2010, and numerous other studies have been published since then.

There is a great interest in developing new highperformance software defect predictors. Besides the interest in developing accurate and robust defect predictors, there is also interest in defining new relevant software features on the basis of which to distinguish between defective and non-defective software modules. A lightweight segmentation network was introduced for the real-time detection of broken strands on power lines, thus enhancing the efficiency of inspection processes [11]. ### reference


Deep Learning is designed to continually analyze data with a logic structure as mimicking how a human can draw a conclusion. The deep learning needs a huge number of data sets to use input in the algorithms in order to result in a more accurate prediction. For instance, Google's AlphaGo, a sharp intellect and intuition game, learns by itself without predefined data. It makes a more specific move and becomes the greatest player of all. Deep Learning defines a new paradigm based on data-driven programming. Since Machine Intelligence or Deep Learning depends on the training data, the accuracy and quality of data play a vital role for public safety using machine learning in autonomous vehicles. (Testing and Quality Validation for AI Software–Perspectives, Issues, and Practices, page 5)

The application of AI in automated code analysis has also led to significant advancements in early vulnerability detection, thereby strengthening security across SE workflows. In particular, [38] highlights the importance of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques in identifying security vulnerabilities and advocating for hybrid systems that enhance detection accuracy. Similarly, [39] emphasizes how Natural Language Processing (NLP) and DL can aid software vulnerability assessments, resulting in improved resource management and more informed risk evaluation decisions. AI has also revolutionized design and development tasks by automating complex processes. Reference [37] presents a deep learning-based technique for transforming graphical user interface (GUI) mock-ups into operational prototypes, thus simplifying the interface design process. In another example, [39] introduces FLASH, a model-based approach to optimize software configurations to enhance speed and resource efficiency. Furthermore, [40] employs the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III) for software re-modularization, refining the software architecture, reducing code modifications, and improving overall consistency. (Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Software Engineering Phases and Activities (2013–2024): A Quantitative Analysis Using Zero- Truncated Poisson Model, page 3)

Many kinds of research attempt to find solutions for the current obstacles of Machine Learning Systems. To draw optimal decision making, approaches such as Fault Tree Analysis, Fuzzy Logic, Metaheuristic Algorithm, and Artificial Neural Network are developed to test with a huge amount of training data by using different algorithms. However, the sufficiency and versatility of Deep Learning systems are based on the accuracy of the test data set. It is difficult to provide adequate support due to the accessibility of test data quality issue. The current Deep Learning systems have various vulnerabilities and their system analysis and defect detection are extremely difficult. Unlike traditional software systems, Machine Intelligence does not have a clear controllable logic and understandability since the process to make decisions rely on the training data. The recent study shows two major vulnerabilities in Deep Learning systems: Software quality from the output of Deep Learning alone is not adequate; and Failure in unseen attacks even though Deep Learning is immune to known types of attacks [18], [19]. (Testing and Quality Validation for AI Software–Perspectives, Issues, and Practices, page 1)

The application of AI in automated code analysis has also led to significant advancements in early vulnerability detection, thereby strengthening security across SE workflows. In particular, [38] highlights the importance of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques in identifying security vulnerabilities and advocating for hybrid systems that enhance detection accuracy. Similarly, [39] emphasizes how Natural Language Processing (NLP) and DL can aid software vulnerability assessments, resulting in improved resource management and more informed risk evaluation decisions. AI has also revolutionized design and development tasks by automating complex processes. Reference [37] presents a deep learning-based technique for transforming graphical user interface (GUI) mock-ups into operational prototypes, thus simplifying the interface design process. In another example, [39] introduces FLASH, a model-based approach to optimize software configurations to enhance speed and resource efficiency. Furthermore, [40] employs the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III) for software re-modularization, refining the software architecture, reducing code modifications, and improving overall consistency. (Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Software Engineering Phases and Activities (2013–2024): A Quantitative Analysis Using Zero- Truncated Poisson Model, page 3)

Table 12 presents, for each classiﬁer c ∈{ DL-FASTAI, Table 12 memaparkan hasil analisis dari beberapa jenis klasifikator dalam penggunaan prediksi kelemahan perangkat lunak berbasis deep learning. Dua variabel utama yang diperhatikan adalah "sensitivity" (Sens) dan "AUC" (Area Under Curve). Sensitivity merupakan ukuran yang menunjukkan kemampuan klasifikator dalam mendeteksi kasus kelemahan yang sebenarnya. Sementara itu, AUC merupakan indikasi performa yang lebih komprehensif, menunjukkan kemampuan klasifikator untuk membedakan antara kasus kelemahan dan non-kelemahan. Dari data yang tersedia, tidak ada informasi yang cukup spesifik tentang nilai-nilai khusus dari Sens dan AUC untuk setiap klasifikator. Namun, perlu diingat bahwa hasil analisis ini mungkin membantu para peneliti memahami pola umum performa antara berbagai jenis klasifikator dalam konteks prediksi kelemahan perangkat lunak dengan menggunakan deep learning. (An in-Depth Analysis of the Software Features’ Impact on the Performance of Deep Learning-Based Software Defect Predictors, page 14)

Problem 'P': (requirement, specification, design, model, analysis, architecture, implementation, code, test, verification, validation, maintenance), and Intervention 'I': (machine learning, deep learning). We have not considered Comparison 'C' and Outcome 'O' as this is out of the scope of this study. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a type of artificial neural network specifically designed to process two-dimensional grid-shaped data, such as images. The convolution layer, pooling layer, and fully connected layer are the three primary hierarchical layers of a CNN. The central component of a CNN is the convolution layer, where different visual elements like edges, textures, and patterns are detected by applying filters or kernels to the input. A feature map reflecting the position of a certain feature in the original image is produced by the convolution layer's filters scanning the entire input. The way that neurons in the human brain react to visual stimuli is comparable to this mechanism. Pada bagian atas skema, terdapat label "Input" dan "Output", yang menunjukkan bahwa gambar ini berfungsi untuk menerima input suatu citra dan menghasilkan output berupa hasil pengenalan atau klasifikasi. Dari skema blok CNN ini, dapat disimpulkan bahwa proses pemrosesan gambar dilakukan melalui beberapa tahap konvolusi dan downsampling dengan maksimum. ### response

Deep learning adalah salah satu teknik machine learning yang menggunakan jaringan saraf tiruan (neural network) untuk mempelajari pola-pola kompleks dalam data. CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) adalah jenis neural network yang khusus dirancang untuk bekerja dengan citra dan video.

Dalam konteks artikel-artikel yang Anda berikan, deep learning digunakan untuk mengembangkan model iYOLOV7-TPE-SS yang dapat mendeteksi kerusakan jalan secara real-time menggunakan CNN. Model ini menggunakan dataset dari sebelumnya dan melakukan optimasi parameter dengan teknik hyperparameter optimization.

Dengan demikian, hubungan antara deep learning dan CNN adalah bahwa CNN merupakan salah satu jenis teknologi deep learning yang digunakan untuk mengembangkan model pengenalan citra, seperti dalam kasus deteksi kerusakan jalan.

1. Deep Learning is designed to continually analyze data with a logic structure as mimicking how a human can draw a conclusion. Deep Learning defines a new paradigm based on data-driven programming. AI has also revolutionized design and development tasks by automating complex processes. However, the sufficiency and versatility of Deep Learning systems are based on the accuracy of the test data set. It is difficult to provide adequate support due to the accessibility of test data quality issue. The current Deep Learning systems have various vulnerabilities and their system analysis and defect detection are extremely difficult. Unlike traditional software systems, Machine Intelligence does not have a clear controllable logic and understandability since the process to make decisions rely on the training data. ### response

Deep Learning adalah metode belajar mesin yang didasarkan pada struktur logika seperti cara manusia menggambar kesimpulan. Ia memerlukan banyak data untuk menggunakan input dalam algoritma untuk menyelesaikan prediksi yang lebih akurat.

Dalam contoh Google's AlphaGo, aplikasi ini belajar sendiri tanpa data yang telah ditentukan dan menjadi pemain terbaik di semua waktu.

Deep Learning juga menggambarkan paradigma baru berdasarkan pengembangan program data-driven. Karena Machine Intelligence atau Deep Learning bergantung pada pelatihan data, akurasi dan kualitas data sangat penting untuk keamanan umum menggunakan pemrograman mesin belajar dalam kendaraan otomatis.

Selain itu, Deep Learning dapat digunakan dalam berbagai bidang seperti penggunaan AI dalam analisis kode yang diotomatisasi, deteksi kegagalan dini, dan peningkatan keamanan di sepanjang alur kerja SE.

### retrieved_context

1. Many kinds of research attempt to find solutions for the current obstacles of Machine Learning Systems. To draw optimal decision making, approaches such as Fault Tree Analysis, Fuzzy Logic, Metaheuristic Algorithm, and Artificial Neural Network are developed to test with a huge amount of training data by using different algorithms. However, the sufficiency and versatility of Deep Learning systems are based on the accuracy of the test data set. It is difficult to provide adequate support due to the accessibility of test data quality issue. The current Deep Learning systems have various vulnerabilities and their system analysis and defect detection are extremely difficult. Unlike traditional software systems, Machine Intelligence does not have a clear controllable logic and understandability since the process to make decisions rely on the training data. The recent study shows two major vulnerabilities in Deep Learning systems: Software quality from the output of Deep Learning alone is not adequate; and Failure in unseen attacks even though Deep Learning is immune to known types of attacks [18], [19]. (Testing and Quality Validation for AI Software–Perspectives, Issues, and Practices, page 1)

2. There are a number of causes affecting the quality of image data [48], [49], such as sharpness, noise, tone reproduction, contrast, distortion, etc. Thus, the typical image quality factors are listed as accuracy, accessibility, readability and understandability, consistency [44], etc.

According to the recent 2018 IEEE NAVIDA AI City challenge [33], manually generating annotated data sets based on image datasets from city street transportation cameras bring diverse data quality issues in a deep learning process. Their case study result clearly indicates that the accuracy and quality of derived AI city transportation programs using a deep learning approach highly depends on the quality of annotated training data sets. Based on their experience report, all of the challenge teams encountered diverse data quality issues in annotated training datasets. And they also discovered the urgent needs in quality validation models, methods, and automatic tools for annotated datasets although there are numerous data validation tools for structure data. Therefore, the key issues of quality assurance for big data applications are how to validate unstructured data quality and how to validate system quality in terms of various quality factors.

Data quality validation and services in a deep learning process for AI software has three dimensions. They are shown as follows.

-Raw data quality checking, which refers to the quality checking process and activities for collected raw data, such as camera-generated images, and videos. The primary objective is to perform raw data cleaning, quality monitoring, and evaluation to ensure high-quality raw data could be collected. -Test data quality evaluation, which refers to test data quality evaluation based on the validation results of a targeted domain-specific application. For a machine learning application system, the major focus of this task should be facilitating AI system quality problem detection, defect improvement, training quality coverage and domain-based knowledge modeling issues for AI systems. (Testing and Quality Validation for AI Software–Perspectives, Issues, and Practices, page 6)

3. In recent years, data (such as image and video image) quality assessment has attracted significant attention. Besides, the quality of big image/video datasets with labeled also have an important impact on machine learning algorithms, such as deep learning. Using a deep learning approach to train artificial AI programs based on annotated training data sets is a popular way to develop intelligent software using a supervised learning approach. With the increasing installation of video cameras in many cities, image data quality assessment is becoming a very hot research topic in computer vision and smart cities. (Testing and Quality Validation for AI Software–Perspectives, Issues, and Practices, page 6)

4. Software Defects Prediction (SDP) consists in identifying defective software components, being considered an essential activity during software development. It represents the activity of identifying defective software modules in new versions of a software system [1]. SDP is considered of great importance in software engineering, as it contributes to continuously improving the software quality. Developing high quality software systems is expensive and, in this context, SDP is used for increasing the cost effectiveness of quality assurance and testing [2]. By detecting fault-prone modules in new versions of a software system, SDP helps to allocate the effort so as to test more thoroughly those modules [1]. (An in-Depth Analysis of the Software Features’ Impact on the Performance of Deep Learning-Based Software Defect Predictors, page 1)

5. With the fast advance of artificial intelligence technologies and data-driven machine learning techniques, how to build high-quality AI software and applications becomes a very hot subject. The special features of AI software bring new challenges and issues for validating software or system quality. Aiming to clarify the primary issues on AI software testing, this paper provides perspective views on AI software quality validation, including the tutorial concepts, test features and focuses, as well as a validation process. Moreover, the primary types of AI software testing and existing validation approaches are analyzed and discussed. The paper also points out the test quality evaluation and coverage problems in AI software. Furthermore, case studies on practical AI software applications are performed to indicate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed quality validation approach. (Testing and Quality Validation for AI Software–Perspectives, Issues, and Practices, page 1)

6. Software quality is defined by how closely a software system meets a desired combination of quality attributes [6], [7]. These attributes include complexity, reliability, scalability, functionality, efficiency, portability, usability, and maintainability, each contributing to the system's overall effectiveness [8], [9]. These quality attributes reflect the actual characteristics of the implemented system [8].

In AI-based systems, quality attributes are critical in shaping architectural decisions [4]. These systems introduce additional challenges, such as model management, accuracy, robustness, and inference latency [3], which the architectural design process must carefully address. Consequently, selecting an appropriate architectural style ensures that AI-based software systems meet their requirements effectively. (Architectural Styles and Quality Attributes in AI-Based Video Software: A Systematic Literature Review, page 1)

7. With the fast growth of artificial intelligence and big data computing technologies, more and more software service systems have been developed using diverse machine learning models and technologies to make business and intelligent decisions based on their multimedia input to achieve intelligent features, such as image recognition, recommendation, decision making, prediction, etc. Nevertheless, there are increasing quality problems resulting in erroneous testing costs in enterprises and businesses. Existing work seldom discusses how to perform testing and quality validation for AI software. This paper focuses on quality validation for AI software function features. The paper provides our understanding of AI software testing for new features and requirements. In addition, current AI software testing categories are presented and different testing approaches are discussed. Moreover, test quality assessment and criteria analysis are illustrated. Furthermore, a practical study on quality validation for an image recognition system is performed through a metamorphic testing method. Study results show the feasibility and effectiveness of the approach. INDEX TERMS AI software quality validation, AI testing, testing AI software. (Testing and Quality Validation for AI Software–Perspectives, Issues, and Practices, page 1)

8. The remainder of the paper is organized as follows. Section II states and formalises the SDP problem, highlighting its importance and practical relevance. An extensive review on existing machine learning-based approaches for predicting software defects as well as the data sets and features used in the SDP literature are presented in Section III. Section IV presents the experimental data and methodology used in our work. Section V details the first stage of our research, which consists in a machine learning-based analysis of the software feature sets' relevance. The performances obtained when applying various defect prediction models are comparatively analysed in Section VI. The threats to validity are discussed in Section VII, while Section VIII highlights the conclusions of our paper and draws directions to further extend our study. (An in-Depth Analysis of the Software Features’ Impact on the Performance of Deep Learning-Based Software Defect Predictors, page 2)

### response

Sistem deep learning memiliki beberapa tantangan software quality, yaitu:

* Kesulitan memberikan dukungan yang cukup karena aksesibilitas masalah kualitas data tes.
* Kemampuan sistem yang bervariasi dan analisis sistem serta deteksi cacat yang sangat sulit.
* Ketergantungan pada kualitas data pelatihan untuk keakuratan sistem deep learning.

(Sumber: Testing and Quality Validation for AI Software–Perspectives, Issues, and Practices)

### user_input

Apa itu software metrics?

### retrieved_context

1. Measurement is needed to validate the effectiveness of software development process. The phrase software metrics describes measurements made on an artifact of software whereas a software artifact has two significant elements: the coded implementation, and the document of its design specification. The initially calculated McCabe, Halstead, and Albrecht metrics, presented during the 1970s, were typically constructed on the coded final software products. Examples of software science metrics include [1] function point analysis [2], and cyclomatic complexity metric [3], which predominated in the early 1980s to measure software product. (Efficacy of Inheritance Aspect in Software Fault Prediction—A Survey Paper, page 1)

2. Software metrics are foundation to quantify complexity, quality of software, and project costs with effort estimation. Function points and cyclomatic complexity are traditional metrics. These are being utilized in the paradigm of procedure language. Nonetheless, these may not merely be utilized in the context of object-oriented [21]. The procedural languages are less complex while comparing with object-oriented programming language [22]. The majority of studies specified hurdles in moving from a procedural approach towards an objectoriented paradigm [23].In object-oriented, it is problematic to comprehend how inheritance, abstraction, and encapsulation associated with each other. (Efficacy of Inheritance Aspect in Software Fault Prediction—A Survey Paper, page 1)

3. Software metrics make it easy for developers to audit and monitor the quality of software design as the project progresses. In addition, predicting the probability of defective classes is needed to help the software engineers during development to enhance the quality of software and reduce testing and maintenance costs. For example, in order to increase the productivity of software testing, software evaluators can plan tests based on the parts most prone to faults.

TABLE 1. List of inheritance metrics.

Software metrics and fault data for an earlier software version are utilized to make an SFP model for the next software version [83]. When a software has faults, it leades to a disaster because it has a significant human dependency on it. Therefore, there is an emerging requirement for software without faults. Software Companies are expanding to discover faults in software. Producing software without faults is a challenging job. To lower costs and improve software usefulness, it is vital to classify classes which are faulty. Many software metrics are proposed by the researchers to gauge the software quality. In object-oriented paradigm, metrics are beneficial for software engineers to make additional information associated with software quality available. Quality of software can also be monitored through metrics, while software evaluators use metrics to increase the effectiveness of testing [84]. (Experimental Validation of Inheritance Metrics’ Impact on Software Fault Prediction, page 3)

4. TABLE 2. Class-level software metric used in this study.

Tabel ini memuat beberapa metrik kelas untuk prediksi kesalahan perangkat lunak. Data tabel menunjukkan bahwa ada dua dataset utama: Software Metrics dan Full Dataset. Kedua dataset tersebut berbeda dalam hal variabel independen yang digunakan, yaitu ESM (Error-Severity Metric) values dan software metrics yang diekstraksi dari modul perangkat lunak.

Pada tabel ini, kita dapat melihat bahwa terdapat tiga jenis metrik ESM: IndexOutOfBounds, NullPointer, dan ClassCast. Masing-masing metrik tersebut memiliki nilai-nilai yang berbeda-beda pada kedua dataset. Pada Software Metrics Dataset, variabel independen hanya mencakup software metrics, sedangkan pada Full Dataset juga termasuk ESM values.

Dengan memperhatikan tabel ini, kita dapat menyimpulkan bahwa peneliti menggunakan metrik-metrik tersebut untuk memprediksi kesalahan perangkat lunak. Pada dataset yang lebih lengkap (Full Dataset), penulis juga melibatkan ESM values sebagai variabel independen tambahan. Hal ini menunjukkan bahwa penulis ingin mengetahui bagaimana pengaruh nilai-nilai ESM terhadap performa model pelatihan machine learning.

Dalam konteks yang lebih luas, tabel ini memberikan gambaran tentang cara peneliti menggunakan metrik kelas untuk prediksi kesalahan perangkat lunak. Penemuan penulis dapat berguna dalam meningkatkan akurasi model pemodelan perangkat lunak dan mengidentifikasi potensi masalah yang mungkin terjadi pada sistem. (Error-Type—A Novel Set of Software Metrics for Software Fault Prediction, page 6)

5. The software metrics are the basis to measure the complexity, quality of software and estimate cost along with efforts of projects. 7. TABLE 2. Frequently Used Metrics in Software Fault Prediction.

Variabel utama di tabel ini meliputi nama penulis, judul penelitian, metode yang digunakan, serta hasil yang diperoleh. Nilai penting dari tabel ini adalah penemuan bahwa beberapa metrik khususnya terkait dengan sifat objek-oriented telah terbukti efektif dalam prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak.

Selain itu, juga terlihat bahwa beberapa penulis menggunakan kombinasi berbagai metode analisis untuk mencapai hasil prediksi yang lebih akurat.

Insight singkat dari tabel ini adalah pentingnya penggunaan metrik-metrik tertentu dalam prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak. Dengan demikian, penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa dengan memahami dan menggunakan metrik yang tepat, kita dapat meningkatkan akurasi prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak. (Efficacy of Inheritance Aspect in Software Fault Prediction—A Survey Paper, page 13)

3. Metrics and roles play a fundamental role in SD, as supported by GAI. The utilization of these metrics enables the establishment of an objective for evaluating the quality of AI-generated codes, including their accuracy and efficiency. These measures empower developers to evaluate the congruence between the resulting artifacts and original objectives, thereby identifying opportunities for enhancement [21], [22]. More broadly, metrics support software engineering quality assessment by quantifying the key characteristics of the development process, including efficiency and maintainability. A review of the literature reveals that commonly reported metrics include structural complexity measures, which assess software architecture using indicators such as the number of modules and interconnections [23]. metrics (23%) or necessary metrics (30%) for software process improvement. The most common metrics are collected by SMEs (30%), large (30%) and very large (11%) organizations as shown in Figure 16. 6. There is a long history of research on metrics programs (MPs) [24], and plenty of literature recommending success factors for their implementation [17], [28], [34], [44]. However, literature on SMEs using MPs in the context of Agile is rather scarce. Moreover, the literature on measuring software processes and their role in improving SME processes is even scarcer. Measuring software processes with the use of process metrics enables objective and quantitative evaluation of software processes, which can lead to continuous improvement and learning [34], [42]. However, measuring process metrics is a challenge [43]. Software processes are inherently complex and intangible, which makes their measurement more difficult than their product counterparts [19], [41]. Ideally, measurement activities should consume little effort and time, while being adequate enough to meet an organization's measurement demands. Software organizations need to weigh in cost-efficiency while prioritizing measurement objectives and targets. SMEs have the added constraints of limited budget, ambitious deadlines, and short-term strategy [45]. 7. Kupiainen et al. [22] conducted a systematic review of the use and impact of software metrics in ASD in industry. The authors reported that software metrics are mainly used for sprint planning, tracking progress, improving software quality, fixing software process, and motivating people. The authors reported that metrics like velocity, effort estimation, customer satisfaction, defect count, technical debt and build are used prominently in ASD. In their systematic review, Tahir et al. [46] observed that metrics for defects, effort, size, duration, productivity, employee commitment, and customer satisfaction are commonly reported in the state of the art. These findings complement another review by Gómez et al. [15], where complexity and size were found to be the most measured attributes in MPs. Other usage of metrics in ASD discussed in the literature are for planning and tracking software development [22], understanding development performance and product quality [48], measuring process quality [50], estimating effort [47], and reporting progress and quality to stakeholders not involved in the actual development [4]. Taken together, metrics targeting sprint planning, fixing software process, effort estimation, development performance, and software defects can be used to measure an organization's process performance. However, this objective is not expressly stated in any of the reviews mentioned above. On the contrary, [22] remarked that more studies are needed to explore the rationale behind utilizing the metrics the authors found in their review. (Measuring and Improving Agile Processes in a Small-Size Software Development Company, page 3)

8. TABLE 2. Class-level software metric used in this study.

Tabel ini memuat beberapa metrik kelas untuk prediksi kesalahan perangkat lunak. Data tabel menunjukkan bahwa ada dua dataset utama: Software Metrics dan Full Dataset. Kedua dataset tersebut berbeda dalam hal variabel independen yang digunakan, yaitu ESM (Error-Severity Metric) values dan software metrics yang diekstraksi dari modul perangkat lunak.

Pada tabel ini, kita dapat melihat bahwa terdapat tiga jenis metrik ESM: IndexOutOfBounds, NullPointer, dan ClassCast. Masing-masing metrik tersebut memiliki nilai-nilai yang berbeda-beda pada kedua dataset. Pada Software Metrics Dataset, variabel independen hanya mencakup software metrics, sedangkan pada Full Dataset juga termasuk ESM values.

Dengan memperhatikan tabel ini, kita dapat menyimpulkan bahwa peneliti menggunakan metrik-metrik tersebut untuk memprediksi kesalahan perangkat lunak. Pada dataset yang lebih lengkap (Full Dataset), penulis juga melibatkan ESM values sebagai variabel independen tambahan. Hal ini menunjukkan bahwa penulis ingin mengetahui bagaimana pengaruh nilai-nilai ESM terhadap performa model pelatihan machine learning.

Dalam konteks yang lebih luas, tabel ini memberikan gambaran tentang cara peneliti menggunakan metrik kelas untuk prediksi kesalahan perangkat lunak. Penemuan penulis dapat berguna dalam meningkatkan akurasi model pemodelan perangkat lunak dan mengidentifikasi potensi masalah yang mungkin terjadi pada sistem. (Error-Type—A Novel Set of Software Metrics for Software Fault Prediction, page 6)

3. In order to effectively coordinate and evaluate software quality management efforts, software companies use software quality models [34], [37], [44], [45]. The earliest software quality model was proposed by McCall in 1976. The McCall model was later revised by Boehm and Dromey [41], [44], [46], [47]. Recently developed software quality evaluation models include ISO/IEC 25010 which outlines 8 attributes to be used for software quality assessment. In contrast, the earlier version ISO/IEC 9126 adopts 6 characteristics [44], [45], [48].

Despite being viewed as a useful tool for quality assurance [44], software standards or models lack functionality and practical application owing to the ambiguity involved [37], [47]. Gorla and Lin as cited in [49] propose a software quality assessment model that includes relevance and usefulness (i.e., functionality), usability, maintainability, and reliability attributes. On the other hand, other scholars identify usability, reliability, functionality, performance efficiency, portability, and maintainability as important quality measurements [40], [46]. Similarly, several studies identify functionality, usability, reliability, performance efficiency, and maintainability as the most impactful measures of software quality [14], [41], [43], [45]. Consequently, functionality, usability, performance efficiency, reliability, and maintainability indicators are adopted for the evaluation of software quality in this study. (How Software Quality Mediates the Impact of Intellectual Capital on Commercial Open-Source Software Company Success, page 1)

4. Metrics and roles play a fundamental role in SD, as supported by GAI. The utilization of these metrics enables the establishment of an objective for evaluating the quality of AI-generated codes, including their accuracy and efficiency. These measures empower developers to evaluate the congruence between the resulting artifacts and original objectives, thereby identifying opportunities for enhancement [21], [22]. More broadly, metrics support software engineering quality assessment by quantifying the key characteristics of the development process, including efficiency and maintainability. A review of the literature reveals that commonly reported metrics include structural complexity measures, which assess software architecture using indicators such as the number of modules and interconnections [23]. Quality metrics are used to forecast software reliability and support decision-making throughout the SDLC [24]. Finally, productivity metrics are reported, and these assess the impact of GAI-based tools on development speed, quality, and overall efficiency [6], [25]. (Generative Artificial Intelligence for Software Development Using ISO/IEC 29110 Basic Profile: Gaps and Opportunities, page 2)

(Generative Artificial Intelligence for Software Development Using ISO/IEC 29110 Basic Profile: Gaps and Opportunities, page 2)

6. Kupiainen et al. [22] conducted a systematic review of the use and impact of software metrics in ASD in industry. The authors reported that software metrics are mainly used for sprint planning, tracking progress, improving software quality, fixing software process, and motivating people. The authors reported that metrics like velocity, effort estimation, customer satisfaction, defect count, technical debt and build are used prominently in ASD. In their systematic review, Tahir et al. [46] observed that metrics for defects, effort, size, duration, productivity, employee commitment, and customer satisfaction are commonly reported in the state of the art. These findings complement another review by Gómez et al. [15], where complexity and size were found to be the most measured attributes in MPs. Other usage of metrics in ASD discussed in the literature are for planning and tracking software development [22], understanding development performance and product quality [48], measuring process quality [50], estimating effort [47], and reporting progress and quality to stakeholders not involved in the actual development [4]. Taken together, metrics targeting sprint planning, fixing software process, effort estimation, development performance, and software defects can be used to measure an organization's process performance. However, this objective is not expressly stated in any of the reviews mentioned above. On the contrary, [22] remarked that more studies are needed to explore the rationale behind utilizing the metrics the authors found in their review. (Measuring and Improving Agile Processes in a Small-Size Software Development Company, page 3)

7. The software metrics are the basis to measure the complexity, quality of software and estimate cost along with efforts of projects. Traditional metrics such as function point and cyclomatic complexity have been employed in the procedure paradigm. But, these are not simply used in object-oriented paradigm [39], [40]. Object Oriented programming is complex while comparing it with procedural languages [41]. Most studies stated difficulty in switching to the object-oriented paradigm from the procedural approach [42]. In Objectoriented Programming, it is difficult to understand how features, for example abstraction, inheritance and encapsulation relate to each other [43]. (Experimental Validation of Inheritance Metrics’ Impact on Software Fault Prediction, page 1)

8. Soini [8] presented a survey to investigate the use of software measurement in the Finish software industry. The problems, challenges, limitations are evaluated. There is an overlap between the metrics used for measuring processes and products and most of the process metrics are used for product measurement too which can affect the effectiveness of decision making. Most of the metrics are extracted from the data that was not collected with the intention/context of measurement. Metrics are not collected for their intended use at some management level e.g., middle or upper management. Most of the metrics are lagging (calculated at the end of a process) but there is a strong need of leading metrics (real-time) that can support effective monitoring and controlling. The metrics selection method is based on the information system available for project management in software organizations, or metrics are extracted from already collected data. The metrics are mostly collected to characterize and evaluate while they are rarely used for prediction and improvement of software processes, products, and resources. Most of the metrics are collected and analyzed regarding processes and products entities while resource metrics are least collected and analyzed. We have also evaluated related issues in Pakistani Software industry including purposes of measurement processes, types of metrics, real-time metrics, scope of measurement process, availability of measurement tools, and defined measurement process (Section 3.1). (An Evaluation of Software Measurement Processes in Pakistani Software Industry, page 3)

5. Software testing plays an essential role in Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) as it ensures the quality and correctness of the software system. Therefore, it is mostly inefficient or impossible to spend the same amount of testing resources and efforts on every individual software module of the system under test. To overcome this problem, Software Fault Prediction (SFP) has been introduced to early identify faulty software modules prior to the testing phase so that the allocation of testing resources can be economically optimised. (Error-Type—A Novel Set of Software Metrics for Software Fault Prediction, page 1)

6. In this study, software metrics have been imported from the BugHunter Dataset and re-validated using Metric-sReloaded [49], which is a tool for obtaining/measuring software metrics from source codes. The software metrics we used in this study are at the class level and can be found in Table 2.

The reasons we employed the BugHunter Dataset are (1) the software metrics were collected from large industrial projects which are still actively maintained; (2) the source codes of the projects are publicly available via GitHub [50] for us to verify the correctness of the collected software metrics and extract the ESM values; and (3) the BugHunter Dataset collects software metrics based on before-fix and after-fix snapshots of the source code elements that were affected by bugs whilst leaving the source code elements that were not affected by bugs untouched. This approach is useful to capture the changes in software metrics when a bug is being fixed. The empirical evaluations showed that the dataset can be used for further investigations such as bug prediction. (Error-Type—A Novel Set of Software Metrics for Software Fault Prediction, page 5)

Variabel utama di tabel ini meliputi nama penulis, judul penelitian, metode yang digunakan, serta hasil yang diperoleh. Nilai penting dari tabel ini adalah penemuan bahwa beberapa metrik khususnya terkait dengan sifat objek-oriented telah terbukti efektif dalam prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak.

Pola penting dapat dilihat dari kemunculan istilah-istilah seperti "C&K metrics" dan "Li and Henry," yang mengindikasikan bahwa ada metrik yang secara konsisten digunakan dalam penelitian-penelitian ini. Selain itu, juga terlihat bahwa beberapa penulis menggunakan kombinasi berbagai metode analisis untuk mencapai hasil prediksi yang lebih akurat.

Insight singkat dari tabel ini adalah pentingnya penggunaan metrik-metrik tertentu dalam prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak. Dengan demikian, penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa dengan memahami dan menggunakan metrik yang tepat, kita dapat meningkatkan akurasi prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak. (Efficacy of Inheritance Aspect in Software Fault Prediction—A Survey Paper, page 13)

8. TABLE 6. Experimental results.

Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa metrik software baru yang disebut Error-Type dapat digunakan untuk memprediksi kegagalan sistem dengan lebih akurat. Dalam eksperimen ini, empat model belajar mesin (machine learning) dipadankan menggunakan dataset SoftWare Metrics dan Full Dataset.

Dari hasil eksperimen, ditemukan bahwa ketika feature selection tidak diaplikasikan, performance model belajar mesin berkurang karena masalah multi-kolinieritas yang menyebabkan pengaruh negatif terhadap hasil akhir. Namun, setelah feature selection diterapkan, masalah ini dapat dihilangkan, sehingga penggunaan metrik ESM yang baru memberikan informasi lebih bermanfaat kepada model belajar mesin.

Dengan demikian, penelitian ini berhasil menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan Error-Type sebagai metrik software baru dapat meningkatkan keakuratan prediksi kegagalan sistem dan meningkatkan performa model belajar mesin. (Error-Type—A Novel Set of Software Metrics for Software Fault Prediction, page 9)

To lower costs and improve software usefulness, it is vital to classify classes which are faulty. Many software metrics are proposed by the researchers to gauge the software quality. The subject metrics are become the approved standard metrics in software fault prediction. PROMISE and D'Ambros [34] are frequently used datasets repositories having these metrics. Both the repositories encompass datasets of about fifty-two percent of the research paper published after 2005 [9]. Since these datasets are publicly available therefore it is frequently used. The other reason is the non-availability of bug's data of industrial software. (Efficacy of Inheritance Aspect in Software Fault Prediction—A Survey Paper, page 4)

8. The prediction of software faults is the subject of several studies. Many techniques have been proposed for predicting a software fault, including Statistical and Machine Learning methods. These are described as:

Statistical methods are used to find a clear mathematical formula that absolutely identifies how classification should be performed. Kapila and Singh [85] used two statistical approaches to carry out his study: Logistic Regression and Univariate Binary Logistic Regression (UBR) which are useful for analysis of data with binary variables. In Bayesian inference [85], the design of the model relates the metrics with the content of software faults and the tendency of faults. The regression analysis is extensively utilized for prediction of bad smell in the code and linear regression in a case where only two classes of the dependent variable exist. The Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) is utilized to control faulty classes and the Radial Base functions are used to classify the faults according to the different categories of faults [87]. Xing et al. defines the significance of the model of Support Vector Machine (SVM). The SVM model can be used for small amount of data. ### response

Software metrics digunakan untuk memprediksi kegagalan sistem (defect) dengan menggunakan algoritma machine learning. Dalam beberapa penelitian, metrik-metrik ini digunakan sebagai variabel independen dalam pembangunan model prediktif untuk menentukan kemungkinan munculnya kegagalan sistem.

Beberapa contoh software metrics yang digunakan dalam prediksi defect meliputi:

* Metrik ESM (Error-Severity Metric) seperti IndexOutOfBounds, NullPointer, dan ClassCast
* Metrik Halstead, McCabe, LoC in structural programming, dan C&K metrics suite
* Variabel independen seperti volume, desain, kode, dan kompleksitas

Algoritma machine learning yang digunakan dalam prediksi defect antara lain:

* Logistic Regression
* Univariate Binary Logistic Regression (UBR)
* Multilayer Perceptron (MLP)
* Radial Base functions
* Support Vector Machine (SVM)

Dengan menggunakan software metrics dan algoritma machine learning, penelitian telah menunjukkan bahwa metrik-metrik ini dapat digunakan untuk memprediksi kegagalan sistem dengan tingkat akurasi yang lebih tinggi.

Apa itu software testing?

### retrieved_context

1. Testing is defined as ''an activity in which a system is executed under specified conditions, the results are observed or recorded, and an evaluation is made of some aspect of the system'' (ISO/IEC 24765, 2006) [6]. In parallel to this definition of testing, a major task of the software development process, software testing is defined as the process of observing and demonstrating the behavior of a software system for compliance with its specifications [7]. As it requires several strategies and techniques with the involvement of several tools and resources, software testing is also considered as a complex task [8]. The background for this study is given below, summarizing the important role of software testing in the software development life cycle, potential impact of software testing strategies, and review studies conducted on software testing. (Evolution of Software Testing Strategies and Trends: Semantic Content Analysis of Software Research Corpus of the Last 40 Years, page 1)

2. Software testing covers several activities of the software development processes starting from the validation of initial requirements through to the acceptance of the end product by the customer [9]. Starting from the requirement specifications, the software testing tasks need to be planned and implemented in different stages of the software development process. Furthermore, software testing needs to be performed during different stages of the software development process for different purposes, such as the testing of the software product lines [10] and the graphical user interface [11]. (Evolution of Software Testing Strategies and Trends: Semantic Content Analysis of Software Research Corpus of the Last 40 Years, page 2)

3. Testing is a comprehensive concept related to the development of each system. In the software engineering discipline, testing is a crucial task of the software development life cycle. In contrast, software testing in any field other than software engineering can be considered as an end-user testing focused on the suitability of a software developed for a specific purpose in this field. For this reason, the multidisciplinary use of software testing makes it difficult to create a specific corpus of software testing studies in the scope of software engineering. In this context, to create a specific corpus of software testing within the scope of software engineering, a methodology including two sequential stages was followed for corpus creation, which included identifying core publication sources for the software engineering field and extracting articles specific to software testing. (Evolution of Software Testing Strategies and Trends: Semantic Content Analysis of Software Research Corpus of the Last 40 Years, page 1)

4. An analysis of the whole software development process reveals that the testing stage has the longest duration and is the most expensive phase [17] involving labor-intensive tasks [18]. As the software testing process is usually performed with limited resources under time constraints, currently, several research studies are being conducted to improve software testing techniques in order to obtain higher-quality and more reliable software products [19]. (Evolution of Software Testing Strategies and Trends: Semantic Content Analysis of Software Research Corpus of the Last 40 Years, page 2)

5. Software testing is usually conducted in the three stages of creating, executing and evaluating the test cases [12], [13]; thus, the creation of appropriate test cases is critical [14], [15]. In other words, the appropriateness of test cases with software features, such as the technology used, the domain in which the software will be used, and the end-user skills is a critical factor in a successful testing process. Matalonga et al. defined the following seven elements to compose a test case: item (product/functionality under test), input (input variables that will stimulate the test item, output (response returned by the test item after receiving a test input), oracle (expected result, predicted behavior under specified conditions based on its specification or another source), result (comparison between the test output and the test oracle), environment (facilities, hardware, software, firmware, procedures, and documentation intended for or used to perform the software testing), and script (procedure specification for manual or automated testing) [16]. (Evolution of Software Testing Strategies and Trends: Semantic Content Analysis of Software Research Corpus of the Last 40 Years, page 2)

6. Software testing plays an essential role in Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) as it ensures the quality and correctness of the software system. However, complete testing of a software system is practically not possible as it consumes an enormous amount of time and resources [1], [2]. Furthermore, faults are normally not distributed uniformly across software modules. Therefore, it is mostly inefficient or impossible to spend the same amount of testing resources and efforts on every individual software module of the system under test. To overcome this problem, Software Fault Prediction (SFP) has been introduced to early identify faulty software modules prior to the testing phase so that the allocation of testing resources can be economically optimised. (Error-Type—A Novel Set of Software Metrics for Software Fault Prediction, page 1)

7. In the software testing stages, the aim is to develop softwareoriented products and services in a systematic and efficient manner, in which a wide range of tasks, methods, and strategies are used. Depending on the type, scope and context of the designed and developed, the methods and strategies  chosen during the software testing stages vary considerably. The findings of this study offer a wide-ranging insight into not only the themes and trends in focus but also the tools, tasks, methods, and strategies specific to software testing. Specifically, the discovered topics reveal that the most focused tasks in software testing are specification, transformation, detection, localization, generation, evaluation, optimization, verification, and prediction. The important background provided by the core tasks highlighted in this study for software testing has also been addressed by previous studies [49]. (Evolution of Software Testing Strategies and Trends: Semantic Content Analysis of Software Research Corpus of the Last 40 Years, page 9)

Testing is a comprehensive concept related to the development of each system. In the software engineering discipline, testing is a crucial task of the software development life cycle. In contrast, software testing in any field other than software engineering can be considered as an end-user testing focused on the suitability of a software developed for a specific purpose in this field. For this reason, the multidisciplinary use of software testing makes it difficult to create a specific corpus of software testing studies in the scope of software engineering. In this context, to create a specific corpus of software testing within the scope of software engineering, a methodology including two sequential stages was followed for corpus creation, which included identifying core publication sources for the software engineering field and extracting articles specific to software testing. (Evolution of Software Testing Strategies and Trends: Semantic Content Analysis of Software Research Corpus of the Last 40 Years, page 1)

An analysis of the whole software development process reveals that the testing stage has the longest duration and is the most expensive phase [17] involving labor-intensive tasks [18]. As the software testing process is usually performed with limited resources under time constraints, currently, several research studies are being conducted to improve software testing techniques in order to obtain higher-quality and more reliable software products [19]. (Evolution of Software Testing Strategies and Trends: Semantic Content Analysis of Software Research Corpus of the Last 40 Years, page 2)

Software testing is usually conducted in the three stages of creating, executing and evaluating the test cases [12], [13]; thus, the creation of appropriate test cases is critical [14], [15]. In other words, the appropriateness of test cases with software features, such as the technology used, the domain in which the software will be used, and the end-user skills is a critical factor in a successful testing process. Matalonga et al. defined the following seven elements to compose a test case: item (product/functionality under test), input (input variables that will stimulate the test item, output (response returned by the test item after receiving a test input), oracle (expected result, predicted behavior under specified conditions based on its specification or another source), result (comparison between the test output and the test oracle), environment (facilities, hardware, software, firmware, procedures, and documentation intended for or used to perform the software testing), and script (procedure specification for manual or automated testing) [16]. (Evolution of Software Testing Strategies and Trends: Semantic Content Analysis of Software Research Corpus of the Last 40 Years, page 2)

Software testing plays an essential role in Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) as it ensures the quality and correctness of the software system. However, complete testing of a software system is practically not possible as it consumes an enormous amount of time and resources [1], [2]. Furthermore, faults are normally not distributed uniformly across software modules. Therefore, it is mostly inefficient or impossible to spend the same amount of testing resources and efforts on every individual software module of the system under test. To overcome this problem, Software Fault Prediction (SFP) has been introduced to early identify faulty software modules prior to the testing phase so that the allocation of testing resources can be economically optimised. (Error-Type—A Novel Set of Software Metrics for Software Fault Prediction, page 1)

In the software testing stages, the aim is to develop softwareoriented products and services in a systematic and efficient manner, in which a wide range of tasks, methods, and strategies are used. Depending on the type, scope and context of the designed and developed, the methods and strategies chosen during the software testing stages vary considerably. The findings of this study offer a wide-ranging insight into not only the themes and trends in focus but also the tools, tasks, methods, and strategies specific to software testing. Specifically, the discovered topics reveal that the most focused tasks in software testing are specification, transformation, detection, localization, generation, evaluation, optimization, verification, and prediction. The important background provided by the core tasks highlighted in this study for software testing has also been addressed by previous studies [49]. (Evolution of Software Testing Strategies and Trends: Semantic Content Analysis of Software Research Corpus of the Last 40 Years, page 9)

Software testing meningkatkan software quality dengan beberapa cara:

* Melakukan verifikasi dan validasi terhadap sistem yang dikembangkan untuk memastikan bahwa sistem tersebut sesuai dengan spesifikasi dan tidak memiliki kesalahan.
* Mengidentifikasi potensi masalah dalam proses pengembangan dan memberikan saran perbaikan untuk meningkatkan kualitas software.
* Meningkatkan kepercayaan pengguna terhadap produk akhir melalui pengujian yang lebih komprehensif dan berulang.
* Mengurangi risiko kesalahan dan masalah yang mungkin terjadi dalam proses pengembangan.

Software testing plays an essential role in Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) as it ensures the quality and correctness of the software system. However, complete testing of a software system is practically not possible as it consumes an enormous amount of time and resources [1], [2]. Furthermore, faults are normally not distributed uniformly across software modules. Therefore, it is mostly inefficient or impossible to spend the same amount of testing resources and efforts on every individual software module of the system under test. To overcome this problem, Software Fault Prediction (SFP) has been introduced to early identify faulty software modules prior to the testing phase so that the allocation of testing resources can be economically optimised. Software testing merupakan bagian dari proses software development. Software testing meliputi beberapa aktivitas mulai dari validasi kebutuhan awal sampai dengan akseptansi produk akhir oleh pelanggan [9]. Tes dilakukan pada berbagai tahap proses pengembangan perangkat lunak untuk tujuan yang berbeda-beda, seperti tes garis produk software dan antarmuka pengguna grafis [10] [11].

Selain itu, Software testing merupakan suatu kegiatan yang terkait dengan pengembangan sistem. Dalam disiplin ilmu teknik komputer, Testing adalah tugas penting dalam siklus hidup perangkat lunak. Di sisi lain, pengetesan perangkat lunak pada bidang luar ilmu teknik komputer dapat dianggap sebagai tes pengguna akhir yang berfokus pada kesesuaian suatu perangkat lunak yang dikembangkan untuk tujuan tertentu dalam bidang tersebut [12]. 

Oleh karena itu, hubungan antara software testing dan software development adalah bahwa software testing merupakan bagian integral dari proses pengembangan perangkat lunak.

Testing is defined as ''an activity in which a system is executed under specified conditions, the results are observed or recorded, and an evaluation is made of some aspect of the system'' (ISO/IEC 24765, 2006) [6]. In parallel to this definition of testing, a major task of the software development process, software testing is defined as the process of observing and demonstrating the behavior of a software system for compliance with its specifications [7]. As it requires several strategies and techniques with the involvement of several tools and resources, software testing is also considered as a complex task [8]. The background for this study is given below, summarizing the important role of software testing in the software development life cycle, potential impact of software testing strategies, and review studies conducted on software testing. (Evolution of Software Testing Strategies and Trends: Semantic Content Analysis of Software Research Corpus of the Last 40 Years, page 1)

Software testing covers several activities of the software development processes starting from the validation of initial requirements through to the acceptance of the end product by the customer [9]. Starting from the requirement specifications, the software testing tasks need to be planned and implemented in different stages of the software development process. Furthermore, software testing needs to be performed during different stages of the software development process for different purposes, such as the testing of the software product lines [10] and the graphical user interface [11].
