### user_input

Bagaimana software metrics membantu efektivitas software testing?

### retrieved_context

1. Software metrics make it easy for developers to audit and monitor the quality of software design as the project progresses. In addition, predicting the probability of defective classes is needed to help the software engineers during development to enhance the quality of software and reduce testing and maintenance costs. For example, in order to increase the productivity of software testing, software evaluators can plan tests based on the parts most prone to faults.

TABLE 1. List of inheritance metrics.

Software metrics and fault data for an earlier software version are utilized to make an SFP model for the next software version [83]. When a software has faults, it leades to a disaster because it has a significant human dependency on it. Therefore, there is an emerging requirement for software without faults. Software Companies are expanding to discover faults in software. Producing software without faults is a challenging job. To lower costs and improve software usefulness, it is vital to classify classes which are faulty. Many software metrics are proposed by the researchers to gauge the software quality. In object-oriented paradigm, metrics are beneficial for software engineers to make additional information associated with software quality available. Quality of software can also be monitored through metrics, while software evaluators use metrics to increase the effectiveness of testing [84]. (Experimental Validation of Inheritance Metrics’ Impact on Software Fault Prediction, page 3)

2. TABLE 2. Frequently Used Metrics in Software Fault Prediction.

Tabel ini memuat beberapa studi terkait penggunaan metrik dalam prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak. Lima belas penelitian yang disebutkan menunjukkan bahwa beberapa metrik telah digunakan secara luas dalam prediksi kegagalan, seperti metrik yang terkait dengan sifat objek-oriented dan perilaku pengguna.

Variabel utama di tabel ini meliputi nama penulis, judul penelitian, metode yang digunakan, serta hasil yang diperoleh. Nilai penting dari tabel ini adalah penemuan bahwa beberapa metrik khususnya terkait dengan sifat objek-oriented telah terbukti efektif dalam prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak.

Pola penting dapat dilihat dari kemunculan istilah-istilah seperti "C&K metrics" dan "Li and Henry," yang mengindikasikan bahwa ada metrik yang secara konsisten digunakan dalam penelitian-penelitian ini. Selain itu, juga terlihat bahwa beberapa penulis menggunakan kombinasi berbagai metode analisis untuk mencapai hasil prediksi yang lebih akurat.

Insight singkat dari tabel ini adalah pentingnya penggunaan metrik-metrik tertentu dalam prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak. Dengan demikian, penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa dengan memahami dan menggunakan metrik yang tepat, kita dapat meningkatkan akurasi prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak. (Efficacy of Inheritance Aspect in Software Fault Prediction—A Survey Paper, page 13)

3. Measurement is needed to validate the effectiveness of software development process. The phrase software metrics describes measurements made on an artifact of software whereas a software artifact has two significant elements: the coded implementation, and the document of its design specification. The initially calculated McCabe, Halstead, and Albrecht metrics, presented during the 1970s, were typically constructed on the coded final software products. Examples of software science metrics include [1] function point analysis [2], and cyclomatic complexity metric [3], which predominated in the early 1980s to measure software product. (Efficacy of Inheritance Aspect in Software Fault Prediction—A Survey Paper, page 1)

4. The software metrics are the basis to measure the complexity, quality of software and estimate cost along with efforts of projects. Traditional metrics such as function point and cyclomatic complexity have been employed in the procedure paradigm. But, these are not simply used in object-oriented paradigm [39], [40]. Object Oriented programming is complex while comparing it with procedural languages [41]. Most studies stated difficulty in switching to the object-oriented paradigm from the procedural approach [42]. In Objectoriented Programming, it is difficult to understand how features, for example abstraction, inheritance and encapsulation relate to each other [43]. (Experimental Validation of Inheritance Metrics’ Impact on Software Fault Prediction, page 1)

5. TABLE 7. Comparison of CK with inheritance metric. TABLE 7. Perbandingan antara CK dengan Metrik Warisan menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan metrik warisan dapat meningkatkan akurasi prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak dibandingkan dengan metrik CK biasa. Data ini diperoleh dari eksperimen yang melibatkan berbagai teknik belajar mesin dan metode klasifikasi.

Beberapa variabel utama yang diuji dalam tabel adalah metrik warisan, metrik CK, dan hasil prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak. Analisis menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan metrik warisan dapat meningkatkan akurasi prediksi sekitar 10-15% dibandingkan dengan metrik CK biasa.

Namun, perlu diingat bahwa data ini hanya berdasarkan eksperimen yang telah dilakukan dan belum tentu dapat diaplikasikan pada konteks lain. Selain itu, tabel juga menyebutkan beberapa sumber referensi yang terkait dengan prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak, seperti penelitian tentang penggunaan jaringan saraf tiruan untuk prediksi kegagalan.

Dalam kesimpulan, data dalam TABLE 7 menunjukkan bahwa metrik warisan dapat menjadi alternatif yang lebih baik dibandingkan dengan metrik CK biasa dalam memprediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak. (Experimental Validation of Inheritance Metrics’ Impact on Software Fault Prediction, page 12)

6. Kupiainen et al. [22] conducted a systematic review of the use and impact of software metrics in ASD in industry. The authors reported that software metrics are mainly used for sprint planning, tracking progress, improving software quality, fixing software process, and motivating people. The authors reported that metrics like velocity, effort estimation, customer satisfaction, defect count, technical debt and build are used prominently in ASD. In their systematic review, Tahir et al. [46] observed that metrics for defects, effort, size, duration, productivity, employee commitment, and customer satisfaction are commonly reported in the state of the art. These findings complement another review by Gómez et al. [15], where complexity and size were found to be the most measured attributes in MPs. Other usage of metrics in ASD discussed in the literature are for planning and tracking software development [22], understanding development performance and product quality [48], measuring process quality [50], estimating effort [47], and reporting progress and quality to stakeholders not involved in the actual development [4]. Taken together, metrics targeting sprint planning, fixing software process, effort estimation, development performance, and software defects can be used to measure an organization's process performance. However, this objective is not expressly stated in any of the reviews mentioned above. On the contrary, [22] remarked that more studies are needed to explore the rationale behind utilizing the metrics the authors found in their review. (Measuring and Improving Agile Processes in a Small-Size Software Development Company, page 3)

7. TABLE 6. Experimental results.

Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa metrik software baru yang disebut Error-Type dapat digunakan untuk memprediksi kegagalan sistem dengan lebih akurat. Dalam eksperimen ini, empat model belajar mesin (machine learning) dipadankan menggunakan dataset SoftWare Metrics dan Full Dataset.

Dari hasil eksperimen, ditemukan bahwa ketika feature selection tidak diaplikasikan, performance model belajar mesin berkurang karena masalah multi-kolinieritas yang menyebabkan pengaruh negatif terhadap hasil akhir. Namun, setelah feature selection diterapkan, masalah ini dapat dihilangkan, sehingga penggunaan metrik ESM yang baru memberikan informasi lebih bermanfaat kepada model belajar mesin.

Dengan demikian, penelitian ini berhasil menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan Error-Type sebagai metrik software baru dapat meningkatkan keakuratan prediksi kegagalan sistem dan meningkatkan performa model belajar mesin. (Error-Type—A Novel Set of Software Metrics for Software Fault Prediction, page 9)

8. TABLE 5. Experimental results.

Dalam penelitian ini, dilakukan validasi eksperimental terhadap dampak metrik warisan pada prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak. Variabel utama dalam penelitian ini meliputi dua jenis dataset: CK-Inheritance dan Inheritance+CK. 

Pertama-tama, proses filtrasi dilakukan untuk memastikan bahwa setiap dataset memiliki jumlah instansi yang cukup besar untuk dilakukan 10-kali validasi silang tanpa penggantian data. Proses ini menghapuskan 25 dataset dari CK-Inheritance dan 28 dataset dari Inheritance+CK.

Selain itu, filter skewness digunakan untuk memastikan bahwa setiap dataset memiliki distribusi yang seimbang antara instansi yang baik dan buruk. Filter ini menghapuskan sekitar enam dataset dari masing-masing jenis.

Dengan demikian, setelah proses filtrasi dan penghapusan data yang tidak relevan, jumlah dataset yang tersedia untuk eksperimen menurun menjadi 30 dataset per jenis.

Pada bagian eksperimen, penelitian ini menggunakan dua tool utama: bahasa R versi 3.4.3 dan R Studio 1.1.383. Penelitian ini juga menggunakan fungsi aktivasi sigmoid untuk mendapatkan hasil yang lebih akurat dalam prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak.

Dengan demikian, penelitian ini menawarkan wawasan terkait dampak metrik warisan pada prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak dan memberikan sumbangsih penting bagi komunitas akademis. (Experimental Validation of Inheritance Metrics’ Impact on Software Fault Prediction, page 9)

Selain itu, filter skewness digunakan untuk memastikan bahwa setiap dataset memiliki distribusi yang seimbang antara instansi yang baik dan buruk. Filter ini menghapuskan sekitar enam dataset dari masing-masing jenis. Dengan demikian, setelah proses filtrasi dan penghapusan data yang tidak relevan, jumlah dataset yang tersedia untuk eksperimen menurun menjadi 30 dataset per jenis. Pada bagian eksperimen, penelitian ini menggunakan dua tool utama: bahasa R versi 3.4.3 dan R Studio 1.1.383. Penelitian ini juga menggunakan fungsi aktivasi sigmoid untuk mendapatkan hasil yang lebih akurat dalam prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak. Dengan demikian, penelitian ini menawarkan wawasan terkait dampak metrik warisan pada prediksi kegagalan perangkat lunak dan memberikan sumbangsih penting bagi komunitas akademis. (Experimental Validation of Inheritance Metrics’ Impact on Software Fault Prediction, page 9)

### user_input

Apa itu systematic literature review?

### retrieved_context

1. A systematic literature review (SLR) was selected as the research method for this study. ''An SLR is a type of secondary study in which primary studies are examined impartially and iteratively to define, interpret, and discuss evidence relevant to the research questions'' [49]. According to Kitchenham [49], [50], an SLR has three main phases: planning, conducting and reviewing the review, as shown in Table 1. Researchers have used the SLR process in several domains [2], [51]- [55].

The authors of this work completed all three phases of the SLR. Inter-rate reliability analyses were undertaken during the initial and final selection phases of the SLR to reduce inter-person bias. The findings of the inter-rater reliability review are discussed in Section 3.2. We followed all of the processes in the three phases of the SLR, as stated in Table 1.

TABLE 1. SLR phases. (Systematic Literature Review on Security Risks and its Practices in Secure Software Development, page 4)

2. FIGURE 1. Steps of the systematic literature review process.

* Simbol lainnya seperti lingkaran dan persegi panjang yang menggambarkan tahapan-tahapan selanjutnya dalam proses tersebut.

Meskipun tidak terdapat angka atau label penting secara eksplisit, namun dapat disimpulkan bahwa gambar ini menunjukkan bahwa sistematis tinjauan literatur dilakukan melalui beberapa tahap yang jelas dan sistematik. Maka dari itu, makna singkat yang dapat ditarik adalah bahwa proses sistematis tinjauan literatur merupakan suatu proses yang terstruktur dengan baik untuk mencari dan menganalisis informasi yang relevan. (Generative Artificial Intelligence for Software Development Using ISO/IEC 29110 Basic Profile: Gaps and Opportunities, page 5)

3. FIGURE 1. Steps of the systematic literature review process.

Gambar tersebut menampilkan langkah-langkah proses tinjauan literatur sistematis dalam format diagram alir. Diagram ini terdiri atas beberapa langkah yang disajikan secara linear, dengan koneksi antar langkah menggunakan garis berwarna biru.

Pertama-tama, gambar menunjukkan langkah persiapan (Preparation), yang mencakup identifikasi topik penelitian dan perumusan pertanyaan penelitian. Langkah ini diikuti oleh langkah pencarian literatur, yaitu proses pengumpulan dan seleksi artikel yang relevan dengan topik penelitian.

Selanjutnya, gambar menampilkan langkah analisis data, dimana hasil dari literatur yang dipilih akan dianalisis untuk mengidentifikasi temuan-temuan penting. Makna singkat dari gambar ini adalah sebagai peta proses tinjauan literatur sistematis, memberikan panduan langkah demi langkah untuk mengembangkan penelitian dan memastikan kualitas hasilnya. (Generative Artificial Intelligence for Software Development Using ISO/IEC 29110 Basic Profile: Gaps and Opportunities, page 5)

4. To present a comprehensive picture of quality for AI-based software, we conducted a systematic literature analysis following the approach by Kitchenham [14]. Systematic literature studies in software engineering can include reviews and syntheses of prior work, enabling researchers to gain an understanding of the state of a particular research subject. The findings of this SLR research should provide a more comprehensive picture of the gaps and support for software quality in the context of AI-based software systems. The following sections conduct key processes such as literature selection, string searches, and data extraction techniques in accordance with the guidelines of Peterson [15]. (Taxonomy of Quality Assessment for Intelligent Software Systems: A Systematic Literature Review, page 2)

5. The SLR was conducted to extract critical success factors, barriers, and implementation practices from the literature. Rockart [38] defined SLR as a method of systematically collecting, analyzing, and reporting data from the literature of a specific research area and questions of interest [38].

The SLR technique was used to search for the most relevant literature by applying explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria for primary studies [38].

We followed the guidelines provided by Rockart [38] to conduct our SLR study. The approach consists of three main phases: planning, conducting, and reporting the review. A thorough discussion of the SLR study conducted for this research project can be found in our previously published articles [25], [63], [64]. (SPIIMM: Toward a Model for Software Process Improvement Implementation and Management in Global Software Development, page 3)

6. In this systematic literature review (SLR), we focused on examining the most reputable and reliable databases available to researchers, as previously mentioned. It is important to note that we allocated publications to specific databases based on the chronological order of the searches conducted, even though some papers might be present across multiple databases. (Taxonomy of Quality Assessment for Intelligent Software Systems: A Systematic Literature Review, page 5)

7. This systematic review follows a structured approach aligned with prior systematic reviews on LLM-based agents in software engineering [1], [13]. The methodology ensures comprehensive coverage of relevant literature while maintaining rigor and transparency throughout the review process. (Methods and Techniques of Agentic Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review, page 3)

8. Table 1. Researchers have used the SLR process in several domain sebagai dasar penelitian ini membagikan beberapa metode dan langkah dalam melakukan Systematic Literature Review (SLR). Secara singkat, SLR adalah metode penelitian yang kompleks, melibatkan tiga fase utama: perencanaan, pelaksanaan, dan tinjauan.

Dalam fase perencanaan, para peneliti harus menentukan topik atau pertanyaan penelitian, serta mengidentifikasi sumber-sumber informasi yang relevan. Mereka juga harus menetapkan kriteria inklusi dan eksklusi untuk memilih artikel-artikel yang akan diintervensi.

Fase pelaksanaan melibatkan proses mencari dan menganalisis artikel-artikel yang telah dipilih berdasarkan kriteria sebelumnya. Para peneliti harus mengidentifikasi informasi yang relevan, mengumpulkan data, serta melakukan analisis untuk mendapatkan hasil yang diinginkan.

Fase tinjauan adalah tahap akhir dalam proses SLR. Pada fase ini, para peneliti akan meninjau dan menganalisis hasil-hasil dari fase sebelumnya. Mereka juga harus memastikan bahwa hasil penelitian mereka tidak memiliki bias atau kesalahan.

Dalam beberapa domain yang telah diidentifikasi oleh peneliti, metode SLR digunakan untuk mengurangi ketidakakuratan dan kesalahan dalam penelitian. Penulis juga menggunakan teknik inter-rater reliability analisis untuk memastikan bahwa hasil-hasil dari fase tinjauan tidak memiliki bias.

Dalam beberapa kasus, metode SLR digunakan dalam beberapa domain, seperti informasi keamanan (security), pengembangan perangkat lunak (software development) dan sebagainya. (Systematic Literature Review on Security Risks and its Practices in Secure Software Development, page 4)

(Generative Artificial Intelligence for Software Development Using ISO/IEC 29110 Basic Profile: Gaps and Opportunities, page 5)

(Generative Artificial Intelligence for Software Development Using ISO/IEC 29110 Basic Profile: Gaps and Opportunities, page 5)

To present a comprehensive picture of quality for AI-based software, we conducted a systematic literature analysis following the approach by Kitchenham [14]. Systematic literature studies in software engineering can include reviews and syntheses of prior work, enabling researchers to gain an understanding of the state of a particular research subject. (Taxonomy of Quality Assessment for Intelligent Software Systems: A Systematic Literature Review, page 2)

The SLR was conducted to extract critical success factors, barriers, and implementation practices from the literature. The SLR technique was used to search for the most relevant literature by applying explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria for primary studies [38]. We followed the guidelines provided by Rockart [38] to conduct our SLR study. The approach consists of three main phases: planning, conducting, and reporting the review. A thorough discussion of the SLR study conducted for this research project can be found in our previously published articles [25], [63], [64]. In this systematic literature review (SLR), we focused on examining the most reputable and reliable databases available to researchers, as previously mentioned. (Taxonomy of Quality Assessment for Intelligent Software Systems: A Systematic Literature Review, page 5)

(Systematic Literature Review on Security Risks and its Practices in Secure Software Development, page 4)

### reference


A systematic literature review (SLR) was selected as the research method for this study. ''An SLR is a type of secondary study in which primary studies are examined impartially and iteratively to define, interpret, and discuss evidence relevant to the research questions'' [49]. According to Kitchenham [49], [50], an SLR has three main phases: planning, conducting and reviewing the review, as shown in Table 1. Researchers have used the SLR process in several domains [2], [51]- [55]. The authors of this work completed all three phases of the SLR. Inter-rate reliability analyses were undertaken during the initial and final selection phases of the SLR to reduce inter-person bias. The findings of the inter-rater reliability review are discussed in Section 3.2. We followed all of the processes in the three phases of the SLR, as stated in Table 1. TABLE 1. SLR phases. (Systematic Literature Review on Security Risks and its Practices in Secure Software Development, page 4)

Systematic mapping or scoping studies are conducted to provide an overview of a research domain through classification. These studies mainly explore the existing literature to investigate the coverage of multiple topics, the frequency of publications, the research trends, and the publication venues where relevant studies have been published [14]. The systematic mapping in the current study mainly follows the guidelines suggested by Petersen et al. [15]. According to the guidelines for systematic mapping studies in SE [15], the essential process steps of the current systematic mapping study were defining the research questions, searching for relevant papers, screening the papers, keywording the abstracts, extracting the data, and mapping, as shown in Fig. 1. Each process step has an outcome and the outcome of the complete process is the systematic map, which is explained as follows [15]: Definition of Research Questions (Research Scope) -The primary goal of a systematic mapping study is to provide an overview of a research area and identify the quantity and type of research and results available within this area. (Systematic Mapping: Artificial Intelligence Techniques in Software Engineering, page 1)

The SLR was conducted to extract critical success factors, barriers, and implementation practices from the literature. Rockart [38] defined SLR as a method of systematically collecting, analyzing, and reporting data from the literature of a specific research area and questions of interest [38]. The SLR technique was used to search for the most relevant literature by applying explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria for primary studies [38]. We followed the guidelines provided by Rockart [38] to conduct our SLR study. The approach consists of three main phases: planning, conducting, and reporting the review. A thorough discussion of the SLR study conducted for this research project can be found in our previously published articles [25], [63], [64]. (SPIIMM: Toward a Model for Software Process Improvement Implementation and Management in Global Software Development, page 3)

Dalam fase perencanaan, para peneliti harus menentukan topik atau pertanyaan penelitian, serta mengidentifikasi sumber-sumber informasi yang relevan. Mereka juga harus menetapkan kriteria inklusi dan eksklusi untuk memilih artikel-artikel yang akan diintervensi.

Fase pelaksanaan melibatkan proses mencari dan menganalisis artikel-artikel yang telah dipilih berdasarkan kriteria sebelumnya. Para peneliti harus mengidentifikasi informasi yang relevan, mengumpulkan data, serta melakukan analisis untuk mendapatkan hasil yang diinginkan.

Fase tinjauan adalah tahap akhir dalam proses SLR. Pada fase ini, para peneliti akan meninjau dan menganalisis hasil-hasil dari fase sebelumnya. Mereka juga harus memastikan bahwa hasil penelitian mereka tidak memiliki bias atau kesalahan.

Dalam beberapa domain yang telah diidentifikasi oleh peneliti, metode SLR digunakan untuk mengurangi ketidakakuratan dan kesalahan dalam penelitian. Penulis juga menggunakan teknik inter-rater reliability analisis untuk memastikan bahwa hasil-hasil dari fase tinjauan tidak memiliki bias.

Dalam beberapa kasus, metode SLR digunakan dalam beberapa domain, seperti informasi keamanan (security), pengembangan perangkat lunak (software development) dan sebagainya. (Systematic Literature Review on Security Risks and its Practices in Secure Software Development, page 4)

### response

Terdapat beberapa langkah dalam melakukan Systematic Literature Review (SLR), yaitu:

* Perencanaan: menentukan topik atau pertanyaan penelitian, serta mengidentifikasi sumber-sumber informasi yang relevan.
* Pelaksanaan: mencari dan menganalisis artikel-artikel yang telah dipilih berdasarkan kriteria sebelumnya, serta melakukan analisis untuk mendapatkan hasil yang diinginkan.
* Tinjauan: meninjau dan menganalisis hasil-hasil dari fase sebelumnya, serta memastikan bahwa hasil penelitian tidak memiliki bias atau kesalahan.

The rapid proliferation of AI-based software projects and the growing reliance on these systems underscore the urgency of examining their quality for practical applications in both industry and academia. This systematic literature review delves into the study of quality assessment metrics and methods for AI-based systems, pinpointing key attributes and properties of intelligent software projects that are crucial for determining their quality. Furthermore, a comprehensive analysis of this domain will enable researchers to devise novel methods and metrics for effectively and efficiently evaluating the quality of such systems. Despite its importance, this area of development is still relatively nascent and evolving. This paper presents a systematic review of the current state of the taxonomy of quality assessment for AI-based software. We analyzed 271 articles from six different sources that focused on the quality assessment of intelligent software systems. The primary objective of this work is to provide an overview of the field and consolidate knowledge, which will aid researchers in identifying additional areas for future research. Moreover, our findings reveal the necessity to establish remedial strategies and develop tools to automate the process of identifying appropriate actions in response to abnormal metric values. 3. • Purpose -Systematic literature review.

• Objective -Peer-reviewed research papers in computer science and software engineering.

• Viewpoint -Software engineers and industry practitioners.

This SLR aims to answer the general question, ''How is quality defined or studied for AI-based software?'' Using the formulated GQM model above, this review focused on AIbased software attributes and attempted to find answers to the following research questions: RQ1: What are the existing approaches for assessing the quality of software systems for artificial intelligence? RQ2: Which measurable attributes of software systems for artificial intelligence, and which statistical or machine learning models are commonly used for estimating the quality of such systems? RQ3: How effective are such attributes and models?

The motivation for RQ1 was to understand what existing research has produced in terms of general approaches to evaluate the quality of AI-based software projects originating from open-source software project sources.

The motivation for RQ2 was to identify which particular subsets of measurable software attributes are used to define the ongoing status of intelligent systems and which methods are commonly used for the quality assessment of such systems.

The motivation for RQ3 was to rank such methods, approaches, and attributes in terms of effectiveness and reliability. (Taxonomy of Quality Assessment for Intelligent Software Systems: A Systematic Literature Review, page 1)

4. This paper presents a systematic review of the current state of the taxonomy of quality assessment for AI-based software. The main goal of this work is to study the field's landscape and consolidate knowledge to help researchers identify further areas of research. Our research is aimed to investigate the following aspects of quality assessment of AI-based software: 1) existing approaches; 2) measurable attributes, statistical and machine learning models used to estimate quality;

3) effectiveness of the found attributes and models. The primary contributions of this work include providing insight into the defined research area through a comprehensive analysis of existing literature and producing a systematic summary.

The paper is structured as follows: Section II describes the protocol used in this research; Section III illustrates the findings of our work; Section IV offers an interpretation of our findings in relation to the research questions characterizing this systematic literature review and provides their critical interpretation; Section V assesses the constraints and numerous shortcomings that may impact the research, while Section VI addresses the questions related to the quality of this work. Section VII draws some conclusions and identifies areas of further research. (Taxonomy of Quality Assessment for Intelligent Software Systems: A Systematic Literature Review, page 2)

7. Evidence-based software engineering prospects motivated the researchers to conduct a systematic literature review. However, the topic of EDI in software engineering is not studied in detail. Fazli and Bittner [17] also used the systematic literature review approach and studied the cultural factors of diversity and its impact on collaborative software development approaches. They analyzed 20 papers and highlighted the issues due to cultural diversity such as differences in communication, decision-making and interaction during collaboration. Menzez and Prikladnicki [18] performed a systematic literature review on team diversity in software engineering. They included only 11 papers in the study and conducted semi-structured interviews to observe the impact of diverse software development teams. They reported on the challenges and barriers faced by team members at the workplace. They concluded that the consideration of diversity and inclusion has a positive impact on software development. Traylor [19] conducted a meta-analytic investigation on the topic of team diversity-process relationships. (Practicing Equity Diversity Inclusion (EDI) in Software Development Teams: A Systematic Literature Survey, page 3)

Systematic literature review membantu analisis Agile software development dengan melakukan:

Namun, detail bagaimana systematic literature review membantu analisis Agile software development tidak jelas dari konteks.

Tahap ketiga adalah desain. Pada tahap ini, Iflexion akan menciptakan rancangan awal dari perangkat lunak yang sesuai dengan kebutuhan perusahaan tersebut. Terdapat juga sub-tahap di dalamnya, yaitu: desain sistem dan desain antarmuka pengguna.

Tahap terakhir adalah implementasi. Pada tahap ini, Iflexion akan menerapkan rancangan yang telah dibuat ke dalam bentuk perangkat lunak yang siap digunakan oleh klien.

Sub-tahap pertama berfokus pada identifikasi kebutuhan perangkat lunak yang sesuai dengan kebutuhan perusahaan, sedangkan sub-tahap kedua mengidentifikasi keragaman dan kompleksitas perangkat lunak. Tahap ketiga adalah desain. Pada tahap ini, Iflexion akan menciptakan rancangan awal dari perangkat lunak yang sesuai dengan kebutuhan perusahaan tersebut. Terdapat juga sub-tahap di dalamnya, yaitu: desain sistem dan desain antarmuka pengguna. Tahap terakhir adalah implementasi. Pada tahap ini, Iflexion akan menerapkan rancangan yang telah dibuat ke dalam bentuk perangkat lunak yang siap digunakan oleh klien. Dari gambar di atas dapat disimpulkan bahwa Iflexion menawarkan layanan pengembangan perangkat lunak enterprise dengan memberikan dukungan selama proses perencanaan, analisis, desain dan implementasi. (Security Assurance Model of Software Development for Global Software Development Vendors, page 19)

More importantly, we can observe an increased interest in software analytics by different players, from large companies like Microsoft and Google [10], [11] to SMEs and startups offering software analytics services (e.g., Tasktop, 5 Kovair, 6 Kiuwan 7 ) and even research projects (e.g., GrimoireLab,foot_7 Q-Rapids, 9CodeFeedrfoot_9 ). (Continuously Assessing and Improving Software Quality With Software Analytics Tools: A Case Study, page 1)

Companies use modern scalable data ingestion technologies (e.g., Apache Kafka, 1 ActiveMQfoot_1 ) together with data visualization and analytics technologies (e.g., Tableau, 3 Microsoft Power BI 4 ) to learn more about their businesses [4]. These technologies have enabled the concept of the real-time enterprise, which uses up-to-date information and acts on events as they happen [5]. This is also the case in software engineering, where software analytics aims at data-driven software development based on software, process, and usage data [6]- [9]. Software analytics has particular potential in the context of modern software development processes such as Agile Software Development (ASD) due to the incremental nature of these processes, which produce continuous sources of data (e.g., continuous integration system and customer feedback). More importantly, we can observe an increased interest in software analytics by different players, from large companies like Microsoft and Google [10], [11] to SMEs and startups offering software analytics services (e.g., Tasktop, 5 Kovair, 6 Kiuwan 7 ) and even research projects (e.g., GrimoireLab,foot_7 Q-Rapids, 9CodeFeedrfoot_9 ). (Continuously Assessing and Improving Software Quality With Software Analytics Tools: A Case Study, page 1)

Pellegrini et al. (P34) argue that many accessibility issues in software projects are due to (1) postponing the implementation of accessibility features by teams that adopt Agile methods (for example, because they adopt the Minimum Viable Product approach), and (2) a lack of knowledge on the implementation of accessibility. Pellegrini et al. (P34) define a set of new responsibilities for roles involved in software development to address this issue. For example, Product Owner should prioritize accessibility from the beginning of the project and produce user stories that take into account disabled people and their needs. Scrum Master should guarantee that the DONE definition covers accessibility. (Operationalizing Human Values in Software Engineering: A Survey, page 19)

• Gupta et al. [27] developed Team Software Process for Secure Software Development (TSP) specifically for software teams to help them create a high-performance team and prepare their work to produce the best results.

• Flechas et al. [28] developed AEGIS (Appropriate and Effective Guidance for Information Security). It first evaluated device assets and their relationships, then moved on to risk analysis, defining weaknesses, threats, and risks.

• Subedi et al. [29] present a security paradigm that extends security development practices in agile methodology to overcome this problem in web application development.

• Sodiya [30] developed the Secure Software Development Model (SSDM), which provides training to stakeholders in software development with adequate security education.

In contrast to traditional software engineering practices that rely primarily on human developers following established methodologies, ASE advocates the use of AI-based agents that have the autonomy to make decisions, write software, run tests, and interact throughout the software engineering lifecycle-a change reflected in recent work on LLM-based applications in software engineering [4], [5], [6], [7]. (Methods and Techniques of Agentic Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review, page 1)

[29] present a security paradigm that extends security development practices in agile methodology to overcome this problem in web application development. • Sodiya [30] developed the Secure Software Development Model (SSDM), which provides training to stakeholders in software development with adequate security education. • Al-Matouq et al. [15] designed a framework Secure Software Design Maturity Model (SSDMM), and the results show that SSDMM helps measure the maturity level of software development organizations. (Security Assurance Model of Software Development for Global Software Development Vendors, page 2)

Brief comparison between traditional and proposed model menunjukkan bahwa hasil penelitian tentang kualitas proses pengembangan perangkat lunak dapat ditingkatkan dengan memperkenalkan metode baru AZ-Model. Variabel utama dalam tabel ini meliputi "Nilai Tradisional", "Nilai yang Diproporsikan" dan "Perubahan". Nilai-nilai yang dikemukakan dalam tabel menunjukkan bahwa nilai-nilai "Sangat Setuju" dan "Setuju" meningkat, sedangkan nilai-nilai "Tidak Setuju" dan "Sangat Tidak Setuju" menurun. Hal ini berarti ada peningkatan responsif positif dari responden terhadap metode AZ-Model dibandingkan dengan proses pengembangan perangkat lunak tradisional. Namun, perlu diingat bahwa tabel tersebut hanya menunjukkan beberapa nilai tertentu dan tidak memberikan informasi yang jelas tentang bagaimana penelitian ini dilakukan. (Improving the Quality of Software Development Process by Introducing a New Methodology–AZ-Model, page 8)

The software engineering industry is undergoing a rapid transformation driven by the emergence of large language models (LLMs) and their use to create autonomous agents that can perform complex software engineering tasks. This paradigm shift, which we call agentic software engineering (ASE), represents a significant rethinking of how software is designed, developed, and maintained [1], [2], [3]. In contrast to traditional software engineering practices that rely primarily on human developers following established methodologies, ASE advocates the use of AI-based agents that have the autonomy to make decisions, write software, run tests, and interact throughout the software engineering lifecycle-a change reflected in recent work on LLM-based applications in software engineering [4], [5], [6], [7]. (Methods and Techniques of Agentic Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review, page 1)

Many Software Engineers face issues of time, cost, and complexity during traditional software development because all components were built within one organization, due to which it takes more time as well as high price. Complexity is another issue in traditional software development because it is difficult to manage all system components within the limited resources like experts, engineers, time, cost, etc. CBSE is a solution to eliminate the drawback of traditional software development by increasing productivity, maintainability and reducing the development time and cost [10]. (Critical Success Factors of Component-Based Software Outsourcing Development From Vendors’ Perspective: A Systematic Literature Review, page 2)

ASD relies on short feedback cycles as a way to provide flexibility and rapid adaptation to market fluctuations. In this context, decisions are also made more frequently. For instance, product releases and the related decisions take place in short intervals, instead of months/years as was the case with traditional software development approaches such as the waterfall model. Popular agile practices such as continuous integration [29] provide a tight connection to development to ensure errors are detected and fixed as soon as possible. The current tendency to shorten feedback cycles even further (e.g., continuously getting feedback from customers and being able to react on that) enhances the potential for software analytics. Continuous software engineering [30], which has its roots in ASD, represents a holistic approach to providing tight connections among all software development activities, including not only integration but also aspects such as business and development (BizDez) and development and operations (DevOps). (Continuously Assessing and Improving Software Quality With Software Analytics Tools: A Case Study, page 3)

Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a type of artificial neural network specifically designed to process two-dimensional grid-shaped data, such as images. The convolution layer, pooling layer, and fully connected layer are the three primary hierarchical layers of a CNN. The central component of a CNN is the convolution layer, where different visual elements like edges, textures, and patterns are detected by applying filters or kernels to the input. A feature map reflecting the position of a certain feature in the original image is produced by the convolution layer's filters scanning the entire input. The way that neurons in the human brain react to visual stimuli is comparable to this mechanism. Several sensors are required for the stereo vision system, including two cameras, an LED, a laser, and LiDAR. The laser sensor has a small beamwidth; thus, it cannot detect road damage in the form of a large hole, necessitating the use of an array of LEDs, lasers, LiDARs, and other sensors [18], [49]. Reconstructing the pothole takes time, whether using an LED array, laser, or LiDAR. Furthermore, 3D road defect reconstruction and stereo vision require well-lit lighting and slow vehicle speeds [17], [18], [50].

Further research used image-processing techniques. Potholes are a form of road irregularity that can be recognized with traditional image processing techniques. To achieve high accuracy, this technique takes numerous steps, including manual image feature extraction and image processing parameter adjustments. As a result, the image frame rate varies depending on traffic circumstances [21]. Some research that investigated road conditions, pavement conditions, potholes, cracks, smart phone sensors, and accelerometers used machine learning techniques such as support vector machines, neural networks, multilayer perceptron, and decision trees [16]. Furthermore, research is being conducted to detect pavement damage using ML algorithms such as support vector machines, artificial neural networks, and random forests [51]. To improve accuracy, ML models require significant computer resources during data processing, which also includes manual feature analysis.

Several studies used deep convolutional neural network (CNN) techniques to automate the simultaneous feature extraction and categorization of objects [41], [52]. This is challenging to incorporate into real-time road defect detection systems. The deployment of CNN models for road damage detection on devices requires a balance between high accuracy and high efficiency [53]. The CNN models perform exceptionally well in terms of high accuracy, precision, recall, and low loss. This requires CNN models with large architecture and competitive computing costs that are inefficient. To do this while maintaining high accuracy, a simplified CNN model configuration setting is required to achieve good CNN model system performance. High efficiency, which is the CNN model system performance, enables it to detect road faults on edge devices with a short inference time. Because the CNN model on edge devices have limited storage capacity, inference time must be considered. Taking this into account, the CNN model offers good system performance and a short inference time for simpler model configurations, but high accuracy is difficult to achieve. To obtain optimal system performance, the CNN model parameters must be properly chosen. When selecting a detection model, there is no definitive answer as to which model has the best performance [31], [53].

Improving system performance in computer vision, object recognition, and classification using CNN models can be achieved through various methods. These include modifying or adding components to the CNN model structure and optimizing hyperparameter selection during CNN model training. The strategy of enhancing the CNN structure aims to improve feature extraction efficiency and model accuracy by modifying or incorporating new components into the CNN architecture. Several studies have focused on enhancing CNN models by modifying or adding components to the existing CNN structure [54], [55], [56], [57], [58], [59]. DenseNet was integrated into the YOLOv4 backbone to optimize feature transfer and reuse. This involved several modifications, such as adjusting the Path Aggregation Network (PANet) [54], introducing New Residual Blocks, applying Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP), modifying the PANet, and utilizing Hard-Swish activation functions [59]. Similarly, researchers have integrated DenseNet blocks into the YOLOv5 backbone to enhance the preservation and reuse of critical feature information. This was achieved by incorporating a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) [56]. Another study introduced a novel framework called Multiple Graph Learning Neural Networks (MGLNN) for semi-supervised learning on graph-based data [55]. Additionally, modifications were made to the YOLO model using the CSPDarknet53 backbone structure, which included Residual Blocks, DenseNet, Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP), and the Path Aggregation Network (PANet) [57]. (iYOLOV7-TPE-SS: Leveraging Improved YOLO Model With Multilevel Hyperparameter Optimization for Road Damage Detection on Edge Devices, page 2)

### response

CNN merupakan singkatan dari Convolutional Neural Network, yang merupakan suatu jenis model jaringan saraf tiruan yang digunakan untuk melakukan pengenalan gambar dan pemrosesan citra. Dalam konteks artikel yang Anda baca, CNN dipakai untuk mendeteksi kerusakan jalan, seperti lubang atau retakan pada permukaan aspal. Model ini dapat belajar dari data citra yang telah dikumpulkan dan membuat prediksi tentang keberadaan kerusakan jalan dengan tingkat akurasi yang tinggi.

FIGURE 6. CNN block diagram. Gambar ini menampilkan skema blok CNN (Convolutional Neural Network). Elemen visual utama adalah beberapa lapisan konvolusi yang dihubungkan dengan satu sama lain melalui proses pemrosesan suatu gambar. Lapisan-lapisan tersebut terlihat seperti kotak-kotak persegi panjang yang berurutan, masing-masing memiliki label yang menunjukkan jenis operasi yang dilakukan: Conv2D (lapisan konvolusi), MaxPooling2D (proses downsampling dengan memilih maksimum nilai), Flatten (mengubah pola input 3 dimensi menjadi array satu dimensi). Pada bagian atas skema, terdapat label "Input" dan "Output", yang menunjukkan bahwa gambar ini berfungsi untuk menerima input suatu citra dan menghasilkan output berupa hasil pengenalan atau klasifikasi. Namun, detail tentang jenis citra yang digunakan sebagai input masih tidak dapat diidentifikasi secara pasti dari gambar ini. Dari skema blok CNN ini, dapat disimpulkan bahwa proses pemrosesan gambar dilakukan melalui beberapa tahap konvolusi dan downsampling dengan maksimum. Fungsi utamanya adalah untuk mengekstrak fitur-fitur penting dalam citra dan menghasilkan klasifikasi yang akurat terhadap suatu tipe objek atau kategori. Perlu diingat bahwa karena hanya ada skema blok saja, detail tentang parameter atau nilai spesifik dari setiap lapisan konvolusi tidak dapat dilihat. Oleh karena itu, interpretasi harus berfokus pada gambaran umum proses yang terjadi dalam CNN daripada detil teknis parametris. Qurishee [71] presented an autonomous pavement condition evaluation employing deep learning, an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), and Raspberry Pi tiny computer technologies, which improves road maintenance and renovation management efficiency and cost effectiveness. A lowcost Raspberry Pi smart defect-detecting camera was set up with the trained SSD MobileNet v1, which can be deployed with a UAV for real-time and remote pavement condition inspection. According to preliminary data, the smart pavement detector camera achieves 60% accuracy at 1.2 frames per second on the Raspberry Pi and 96% accuracy at 13.8 frames per second on a CPU-based computer. Hassan et al. [72] employs CNN models that are improved tiny YOLO V3 on UAVs and achieves good results, with precision, sensitivity, and F1 score values better than 85%, but without considering FPS. Sathvik et al. [39] introduce TABLE 1. Comparison of object detection models deployed on edge device. pothole detection, an edge computing framework that runs efficient deep neural networks, lowering the latency of earlier techniques. Using transfer learning-based models, an F1 score of 0.64. The YOLO V7 model had an F1 score of 0.51, which improved proportionally (the higher the F1 score, the more efficient the training model) as the number of epochs increased. The YOLO V7 runs on a CPU-based computer, however it does not consider run on edge devices. Several studies using CNN models deployed on NVIDIA Jetson Nano devices include the SSD-MobileNet model with a batch size of 64 and mAP of 0.22 [48], the MobileNet V2 model, and the SSD Resnet50V1 model [34], [35]. The MobileNet V2 model using hyperparameter settings has a higher mAP of 0.0869 and average recall 0.241 than the SSD Resnet50V1. Yebes et al. [40] created a massive dataset of images with pothole annotations and road scenes from many cities across the world, captured with various cameras, vehicles, and viewpoints under varying environmental circumstances. Their fine-tuned Faster R-CNN Inception v2, Faster R-CNN Resnet101, and Faster R-CNN Inception-Resnet v2 models reached precision 75%, and their CNN model deployed the pothole detector on the Nvidia DrivePX2 platform running at 5-6 frames per second. Based on the findings of this investigation, CNN models were included in the hardware, as indicated in Table 1, although further research is needed to improve system performance (mAP, AR, F1 score) and speed up inference time. Based on previous studies on road damage, several researchers have utilized the CNN model by optimizing its network structure. Specifically, the YOLO model automates the network structure through the introduction of a new module. However, few YOLOv3 models incorporate hyperparameter optimization, with only one study utilizing the Bayesian method. (iYOLOV7-TPE-SS: Leveraging Improved YOLO Model With Multilevel Hyperparameter Optimization for Road Damage Detection on Edge Devices, page 1)

The Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model is trained using the prepared dataset. CNN is a type of deep neural network that is highly effective for the analysis and processing of visual data such as images and videos. In this context, CNN is used to predict the position of the ball based on the position data that has been collected during the training session. The training process involves adjusting the weights of the model through the backpropagation technique to minimize the prediction error. The Fig. 7 is a sequential model of the CNN architecture for ball position prediction. A sequential model is a series of layers that are processed sequentially from input to output. The given model consists of several types of layers: Conv1D, AveragePooling1D, Dropout, MaxPooling1D, Flatten, and Dense. The operation process is in equations ( 4) to (9). (Prediction of Ball Position Using CNN Methods With Zed Camera on Goalkeeper Robot Application, page 7)

FIGURE 8. Confusion matrix result of ball detection using CNN. FIGURE 8. Confusion Matrix Hasil Deteksi Bola Menggunakan CNN. Gambar ini menampilkan sebuah grafik yang disebut "confusion matrix". Grafik ini digunakan untuk mengukur akurasi model klasifikasi, yaitu model CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) dalam deteksi bola. Terdapat empat sudut dalam grafik: TP (True Positive), FP (False Positive), TN (True Negative), dan FN (False Negative). Gambar menunjukkan bahwa di bagian atas kiri terdapat nilai 85, yang kemungkinan besar mewakili jumlah kejadian TP. Nilai ini mungkin merupakan akurasi model CNN dalam mendeteksi bola dengan tepat. Di bawahnya, ada label "Recall" dengan nilai sekitar 88%, menunjukkan bahwa model dapat mendeteksi bola dengan tingkat akuransi yang tinggi. Di bagian kanan atas terdapat nilai 15, mungkin merupakan jumlah kejadian FP (False Positive), yaitu kesalahan dalam mengidentifikasi objek sebagai bola padahal sebenarnya bukan. Di bawahnya ada label "Precision" dengan nilai sekitar 97%, menunjukkan bahwa model dapat membedakan bola dari non-bola dengan tingkat akuransi yang sangat tinggi. Di bagian bawah kiri terdapat label "F1-score" dengan nilai sekitar 91%, ini merupakan skor yang dihitung berdasarkan recall dan precision untuk memberikan gambaran lebih komprehensif tentang akurasi model. (Prediction of Ball Position Using CNN Methods With Zed Camera on Goalkeeper Robot Application, page 10)

This research uses the ROS system because it has the ability to integrate camera sensors with artificial intelligence methods and several other combined sensors in the robot. Fig. 4 shows the basic communication system for accessing the ZED camera on the robot. Image information is acquired over time and processed in real-time. The prediction system that has been created using the CNN algorithm tries to change the layer parameter model to get the best results in classifying the position of the predicted direction of the ball. The dataset was collected as shown in Fig. 6. The CNN design used is as in Fig. 7 and equations ( 4) to (9). Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a type of artificial neural network specifically designed to process two-dimensional grid-shaped data, such as images. The convolution layer, pooling layer, and fully connected layer are the three primary hierarchical layers of a CNN. The central component of a CNN is the convolution layer, where different visual elements like edges, textures, and patterns are detected by applying filters or kernels to the input. A feature map reflecting the position of a certain feature in the original image is produced by the convolution layer's filters scanning the entire input. The way that neurons in the human brain react to visual stimuli is comparable to this mechanism. (Prediction of Ball Position Using CNN Methods With Zed Camera on Goalkeeper Robot Application, page 4)

5. The road damage detection research makes use of laser sensors to rebuild 3D road damage as well as stereo vision technologies. Several sensors are required for the stereo vision system, including two cameras, an LED, a laser, and LiDAR. The laser sensor has a small beamwidth; thus, it cannot detect road damage in the form of a large hole, necessitating the use of an array of LEDs, lasers, LiDARs, and other sensors [18], [49]. Reconstructing the pothole takes time, whether using an LED array, laser, or LiDAR. Furthermore, 3D road defect reconstruction and stereo vision require well-lit lighting and slow vehicle speeds [17], [18], [50].

Further research used image-processing techniques. Potholes are a form of road irregularity that can be recognized with traditional image processing techniques. To achieve high accuracy, this technique takes numerous steps, including manual image feature extraction and image processing parameter adjustments. As a result, the image frame rate varies depending on traffic circumstances [21]. Some research that investigated road conditions, pavement conditions, potholes, cracks, smart phone sensors, and accelerometers used machine learning techniques such as support vector machines, neural networks, multilayer perceptron, and decision trees [16]. Furthermore, research is being conducted to detect pavement damage using ML algorithms such as support vector machines, artificial neural networks, and random forests [51]. To improve accuracy, ML models require significant computer resources during data processing, which also includes manual feature analysis.

Improving system performance in computer vision, object recognition, and classification using CNN models can be achieved through various methods. These include modifying or adding components to the CNN model structure and optimizing hyperparameter selection during CNN model training. The strategy of enhancing the CNN structure aims to improve feature extraction efficiency and model accuracy by modifying or incorporating new components into the CNN architecture. Several studies have focused on enhancing CNN models by modifying or adding components to the existing CNN structure [54], [55], [56], [57], [58], [59]. DenseNet was integrated into the YOLOv4 backbone to optimize feature transfer and reuse. This involved several modifications, such as adjusting the Path Aggregation Network (PANet) [54], introducing New Residual Blocks, applying Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP), modifying the PANet, and utilizing Hard-Swish activation functions [59]. Similarly, researchers have integrated DenseNet blocks into the YOLOv5 backbone to enhance the preservation and reuse of critical feature information. This was achieved by incorporating a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) [56]. Another study introduced a novel framework called Multiple Graph Learning Neural Networks (MGLNN) for semi-supervised learning on graph-based data [55]. Additionally, modifications were made to the YOLO model using the CSPDarknet53 backbone structure, which included Residual Blocks, DenseNet, Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP), and the Path Aggregation Network (PANet) [57]. 7. • Proposing a system for predicting the position of the ball using the ZED camera because the ZED camera has the ability to detect ball objects with extreme lighting conditions on the Goalkeeper Robot Application.

• Proposing a system for predicting the ball's arrival position relative to the robot keeper using CNN. By accurately predicting the ball's trajectory, the robot keeper can better position itself to block incoming balls, thereby increasing its defensive capabilities. CNN was chosen because it can learn features automatically and is easy to integrate with low computing specifications in real-time. The best system performance is obtained by comparing several variations of the CNN method.

The CNN method is also used for several mobile robot-vision applications [26], [27] such as service robots or collaboration of several industrial robots [28], [29]. This research aims to build a combination of ZED camera devices with CNN methods that have been used in previous research to detect and predict the position of the ball in the goal area. This model scenario is to be able to reach all lighting conditions with a camera that has artificial intelligence features. The CNN model as an intelligence feature is added so that the system can predict the position of the ball with a ZED camera that has features that can overcome changes in light intensity levels. CNN dapat mengekstrak fitur-fitur visual kompleks dari data citra yang diambil oleh kamera, sehingga cocok digunakan untuk aplikasi seperti deteksi posisi bola dalam waktu nyata pada robot penjaga gawang. Selain itu, CNN juga dapat diproses dalam dua dimensi, sehingga dapat digunakan untuk beberapa aplikasi mobot-vision lainnya seperti service robots atau kolaborasi industri.

The road damage detection research makes use of laser sensors to rebuild 3D road damage as well as stereo vision technologies. Several sensors are required for the stereo vision system, including two cameras, an LED, a laser, and LiDAR. The laser sensor has a small beamwidth; thus, it cannot detect road damage in the form of a large hole, necessitating the use of an array of LEDs, lasers, LiDARs, and other sensors [18], [49]. Reconstructing the pothole takes time, whether using an LED array, laser, or LiDAR. Furthermore, 3D road defect reconstruction and stereo vision require well-lit lighting and slow vehicle speeds [17], [18], [50]. Further research used image-processing techniques. Potholes are a form of road irregularity that can be recognized with traditional image processing techniques. To achieve high accuracy, this technique takes numerous steps, including manual image feature extraction and image processing parameter adjustments. As a result, the image frame rate varies depending on traffic circumstances [21]. Some research that investigated road conditions, pavement conditions, potholes, cracks, smart phone sensors, and accelerometers used machine learning techniques such as support vector machines, neural networks, multilayer perceptron, and decision trees [16]. Furthermore, research is being conducted to detect pavement damage using ML algorithms such as support vector machines, artificial neural networks, and random forests [51]. To improve accuracy, ML models require significant computer resources during data processing, which also includes manual feature analysis. Several studies used deep convolutional neural network (CNN) techniques to automate the simultaneous feature extraction and categorization of objects [41], [52]. This is challenging to incorporate into real-time road defect detection systems. The deployment of CNN models for road damage detection on devices requires a balance between high accuracy and high efficiency [53]. The use of CNN models for road damage detection on devices requires achieving a balance between high accuracy and high efficiency. The use of CNN models for road damage detection on devices necessitates striking a balance between high accuracy and high efficiency. The parameter system performance deployment model CNN on devices performs well in terms of precision, recall, F1-score, and as well as efficiency of time inference. The CNN models perform exceptionally well in terms of high accuracy, precision, recall, and low loss. This requires CNN models with large architecture and competitive computing costs that are inefficient. To do this while maintaining high accuracy, a simplified CNN model configuration setting is required to achieve good CNN model system performance. High efficiency, which is the CNN model system performance, enables it to detect road faults on edge devices with a short inference time. Because the CNN model on edge devices have limited storage capacity, inference time must be considered. Taking this into account, the CNN model offers good system performance and a short inference time for simpler model configurations, but high accuracy is difficult to achieve. To obtain optimal system performance, the CNN model parameters must be properly chosen. When selecting a detection model, there is no definitive answer as to which model has the best performance [31], [53]. Improving system performance in computer vision, object recognition, and classification using CNN models can be achieved through various methods. These include modifying or adding components to the CNN model structure and optimizing hyperparameter selection during CNN model training. The strategy of enhancing the CNN structure aims to improve feature extraction efficiency and model accuracy by modifying or incorporating new components into the CNN architecture. Several studies have focused on enhancing CNN models by modifying or adding components to the existing CNN structure [54], [55], [56], [57], [58], [59]. DenseNet was integrated into the YOLOv4 backbone to optimize feature transfer and reuse. This involved several modifications, such as adjusting the Path Aggregation Network (PANet) [54], introducing New Residual Blocks, applying Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP), modifying the PANet, and utilizing Hard-Swish activation functions [59]. Similarly, researchers have integrated DenseNet blocks into the YOLOv5 backbone to enhance the preservation and reuse of critical feature information. This was achieved by incorporating a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) [56]. Another study introduced a novel framework called Multiple Graph Learning Neural Networks (MGLNN) for semi-supervised learning on graph-based data [55]. Additionally, modifications were made to the YOLO model using the CSPDarknet53 backbone structure, which included Residual Blocks, DenseNet, Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP), and the Path Aggregation Network (PANet) [57]. (iYOLOV7-TPE-SS: Leveraging Improved YOLO Model With Multilevel Hyperparameter Optimization for Road Damage Detection on Edge Devices, page 2)

The convolution layer, pooling layer, and fully connected layer are the three primary hierarchical layers of a CNN. The central component of a CNN is the convolution layer, where different visual elements like edges, textures, and patterns are detected by applying filters or kernels to the input. A feature map reflecting the position of a certain feature in the original image is produced by the convolution layer's filters scanning the entire input. The way that neurons in the human brain react to visual stimuli is comparable to this mechanism. 5. The pooling layer, which comes after the convolution layer, is meant to combine key information and lower the dimensionality of the feature map. Max pooling, which chooses the maximum value within each condensed area of the feature map, is a frequently used kind of pooling. This lessens the number of parameters that must be computed and increases the model's resistance to slight variations in the input features' locations.

CNNs typically have multiple sets of successive convolution and pooling layers, which allow the network to detect increasingly complex features at each layer. Early layers may detect simple edges and lines, while deeper layers may detect more complex objects, such as specific shapes and patterns.

The final input is supplied into the fully connected layer after passing through several convolution and pooling layers. Every neuron in this layer is connected to every other neuron in the layer before it, enabling the network to compile the features that were taken out of the earlier levels and come to a conclusion. An activation function that aids in the final classification, such as ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit) or Softmax, typically follows this completely connected layer.

This study designs and implements appropriate parameter values in each layer of the CNN used. Previous researchers have created several methods for artificial intelligence that have been tried to be implemented on the ERSOW robot. These methods are Label Propagation, Extra Tree Classifier, Ridge Classifier, Linear SVC, Passive Aggressive Classifier, AdaBoost, Label Spreading, Nearest Centroid, GaussianNB, and Dummy Classifier (Prediction of Ball Position Using CNN Methods With Zed Camera on Goalkeeper Robot Application, page 5)

8. This chapter discusses the results of the dataset that has been created as well as the results of the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) testing that has been carried out. In this research, we produced a comprehensive dataset specifically designed for applications involving wheeled soccer goalkeeper robots. The dataset includes a variety of scenarios capturing different ball movements, speeds, shooting angles, and environmental conditions to ensure robustness and versatility.

The development, implementation, and compilation processes in this study were performed on a system with the specifications listed in Table 2. These specifications include various hardware components such as high-performance CPUs, GPUs, and adequate RAM, as well as software components including operating systems, deep learning frameworks, and data processing libraries. The choice of hardware and software was critical to achieve optimal performance, enabling efficient handling of complex algorithms and large volumes of data during the development, testing, and evaluation phases.

Using the right hardware ensured fast processing times and the ability to run intensive computations necessary for training deep learning models. Meanwhile, the selection of appropriate software provided the tools needed for data preprocessing, model training, and evaluation. For instance, the use of deep learning frameworks like TensorFlow facilitated the construction and training of the CNN model, while data processing libraries such as NumPy and Pandas were essential for managing and manipulating the dataset.

At epochs 0 to 20, training accuracy jumps significantly followed by a similar increase in validation accuracy. Testing was conducted to evaluate the performance of the trained model. Table 3 presents the performance report of the proposed model, a CNN-based machine learning model, in classifying test data into three categories: ''right,'' ''left,'' and ''center.'' With 180 test samples, the model achieved an overall accuracy of 70%, indicating that 70% of its predictions were correct. Table 3 shows the result of proposed method and other comparison models. From the performance evaluation results of the CNN prediction model for ball position, it was found that the model performed well for the prediction of the ''right'' and ''left'' classes, with F1-score of 0.84 and 0.76 respectively, indicating that the model was quite reliable in classifying both classes. However, the model performance for the ''center'' class showed a significant decrease, with an F1-score of only 0.39. This suggests either an imbalance in the data or a complexity in the ball movement pattern at the center that is difficult for the model to identify.

These findings show that while the CNN model is effective for most scenarios, there are areas that require improvement, especially in predicting the ''center'' class. One of the future development plans is to improve the data distribution by rebalancing the dataset so that the ''center'' class has more training examples. In addition, more complex models will be developed using other deep learning techniques, such as integration with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to better capture temporal patterns in ball movement.

For the future, some other approaches that can be developed include the use of data augmentation to generate more variations of the ball position in the ''center'' class, as well as further tuning the CNN architecture to reduce the overfitting phenomenon detected in some epochs during training. The use of attention mechanisms can also be implemented to help the model focus on key features of the ball movement, so as to improve prediction accuracy, especially in the ''center'' class which tends to be less accurate. (Prediction of Ball Position Using CNN Methods With Zed Camera on Goalkeeper Robot Application, page 9)

### response

CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) adalah salah satu jenis jaringan saraf tiruan yang khusus dirancang untuk memproses data berdimensi grid, seperti citra atau gambar. CNN menggunakan lapisan konvolusi dan pooling untuk mengekstrak fitur-fitur penting dalam citra dan menghasilkan klasifikasi yang akurat terhadap suatu tipe objek atau kategori.

Dalam konteks penelitian tentang prediksi posisi bola menggunakan ZED camera, CNN digunakan sebagai algoritma pemrosesan citra untuk mendeteksi posisi bola dan memprediksikan arah gerakannya. CNN juga digunakan dalam beberapa aplikasi lainnya seperti pengenalan emosi bahasa, pengenalan wajah, dan pengenalan pola.

Deep learning adalah sebuah cabang ilmu komputer yang berfokus pada pengembangan jaringan saraf tiruan yang dapat belajar dari data dan mengadaptasi diri untuk meningkatkan akurasi hasilnya. CNN adalah salah satu contoh aplikasi deep learning yang digunakan dalam beberapa bidang seperti citra, bahasa, dan audio.

Dalam konteks ini, hubungan antara CNN dan deep learning adalah bahwa CNN merupakan salah satu jenis jaringan saraf tiruan yang dapat digunakan untuk melakukan deep learning, yaitu belajar dari data dan mengadaptasi diri untuk meningkatkan akurasi hasilnya.

The pooling layer, which comes after the convolution layer, is meant to combine key information and lower the dimensionality of the feature map. Max pooling, which chooses the maximum value within each condensed area of the feature map, is a frequently used kind of pooling. This lessens the number of parameters that must be computed and increases the model's resistance to slight variations in the input features' locations. CNNs typically have multiple sets of successive convolution and pooling layers, which allow the network to detect increasingly complex features at each layer. Early layers may detect simple edges and lines, while deeper layers may detect more complex objects, such as specific shapes and patterns. The final input is supplied into the fully connected layer after passing through several convolution and pooling layers. Every neuron in this layer is connected to every other neuron in the layer before it, enabling the network to compile the features that were taken out of the earlier levels and come to a conclusion. An activation function that aids in the final classification, such as ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit) or Softmax, typically follows this completely connected layer. This study designs and implements appropriate parameter values in each layer of the CNN used. Previous researchers have created several methods for artificial intelligence that have been tried to be implemented on the ERSOW robot. This chapter discusses the results of the dataset that has been created as well as the results of the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) testing that has been carried out. In this research, we produced a comprehensive dataset specifically designed for applications involving wheeled soccer goalkeeper robots. The dataset includes a variety of scenarios capturing different ball movements, speeds, shooting angles, and environmental conditions to ensure robustness and versatility. The development, implementation, and compilation processes in this study were performed on a system with the specifications listed in Table 2. These specifications include various hardware components such as high-performance CPUs, GPUs, and adequate RAM, as well as software components including operating systems, deep learning frameworks, and data processing libraries. The choice of hardware and software was critical to achieve optimal performance, enabling efficient handling of complex algorithms and large volumes of data during the development, testing, and evaluation phases. Using the right hardware ensured fast processing times and the ability to run intensive computations necessary for training deep learning models. Meanwhile, the selection of appropriate software provided the tools needed for data preprocessing, model training, and evaluation. For instance, the use of deep learning frameworks like TensorFlow facilitated the construction and training of the CNN model, while data processing libraries such as NumPy and Pandas were essential for managing and manipulating the dataset. At epochs 0 to 20, training accuracy jumps significantly followed by a similar increase in validation accuracy. At epochs 21 to 40, there is a slight increase in training accuracy with a short period of decline before rising again, while validation accuracy rises significantly and then falls sharply before rising again. At epochs 41 to 60, both graphs show steady fluctuations. At epochs 61 to 80, the fluctuation pattern continued on both graphs. At the last epochs, 81 to 100, there is a significant drop in training accuracy followed immediately by a rapid rise, while validation accuracy shows a continuous up and down trend with no apparent stability. Testing was conducted to evaluate the performance of the trained model. Table 3 presents the performance report of the proposed model, a CNN-based machine learning model, in classifying test data into three categories: ''right,'' ''left,'' and ''center.'' With 180 test samples, the model achieved an overall accuracy of 70%, indicating that 70% of its predictions were correct. Table 3 shows the result of proposed method and other comparison models. From the performance evaluation results of the CNN prediction model for ball position, it was found that the model performed well for the prediction of the ''right'' and ''left'' classes, with F1-score of 0.84 and 0.76 respectively, indicating that the model was quite reliable in classifying both classes. However, the model performance for the ''center'' class showed a significant decrease, with an F1-score of only 0.39. This suggests either an imbalance in the data or a complexity in the ball movement pattern at the center that is difficult for the model to identify. These findings show that while the CNN model is effective for most scenarios, there are areas that require improvement, especially in predicting the ''center'' class. One of the future development plans is to improve the data distribution by rebalancing the dataset so that the ''center'' class has more training examples. In addition, more complex models will be developed using other deep learning techniques, such as integration with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to better capture temporal patterns in ball movement. For the future, some other approaches that can be developed include the use of data augmentation to generate more variations of the ball position in the ''center'' class, as well as further tuning the CNN architecture to reduce the overfitting phenomenon detected in some epochs during training. The use of attention mechanisms can also be implemented to help the model focus on key features of the ball movement, so as to improve prediction accuracy, especially in the ''center'' class which tends to be less accurate. (Prediction of Ball Position Using CNN Methods With Zed Camera on Goalkeeper Robot Application, page 9)

Table 3 presents the performance report of the proposed model, a CNN-based machine learning model, in classifying test data into three categories: ''right,'' ''left,'' and ''center.'' With 180 test samples, the model achieved an overall accuracy of 70%, indicating that 70% of its predictions were correct. Table 3 shows the result of proposed method and other comparison models. From the performance evaluation results of the CNN prediction model for ball position, it was found that the model performed well for the prediction of the ''right'' and ''left'' classes, with F1-score of 0.84 and 0.76 respectively, indicating that the model was quite reliable in classifying both classes. However, the model performance for the ''center'' class showed a significant decrease, with an F1-score of only 0.39. This suggests either an imbalance in the data or a complexity in the ball movement pattern at the center that is difficult for the model to identify.

These findings show that while the CNN model is effective for most scenarios, there are areas that require improvement, especially in predicting the ''center'' class. One of the future development plans is to improve the data distribution by rebalancing the dataset so that the ''center'' class has more training examples. In addition, more complex models will be developed using other deep learning techniques, such as integration with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to better capture temporal patterns in ball movement.

For the future, some other approaches that can be developed include the use of data augmentation to generate more variations of the ball position in the ''center'' class, as well as further tuning the CNN architecture to reduce the overfitting phenomenon detected in some epochs during training. The use of attention mechanisms can also be implemented to help the model focus on key features of the ball movement, so as to improve prediction accuracy, especially in the ''center'' class which tends to be less accurate.
