8. The pooling layer, which comes after the convolution layer, is meant to combine key information and lower the dimensionality of the feature map. Max pooling, which chooses the maximum value within each condensed area of the feature map, is a frequently used kind of pooling. This lessens the number of parameters that must be computed and increases the model's resistance to slight variations in the input features' locations.

CNNs typically have multiple sets of successive convolution and pooling layers, which allow the network to detect increasingly complex features at each layer. Early layers may detect simple edges and lines, while deeper layers may detect more complex objects, such as specific shapes and patterns.

The final input is supplied into the fully connected layer after passing through several convolution and pooling layers. Every neuron in this layer is connected to every other neuron in the layer before it, enabling the network to compile the features that were taken out of the earlier levels and come to a conclusion. An activation function that aids in the final classification, such as ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit) or Softmax, typically follows this completely connected layer.

This study designs and implements appropriate parameter values in each layer of the CNN used. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a type of artificial neural network specifically designed to process two-dimensional grid-shaped data, such as images. The convolution layer, pooling layer, and fully connected layer are the three primary hierarchical layers of a CNN. The central component of a CNN is the convolution layer, where different visual elements like edges, textures, and patterns are detected by applying filters or kernels to the input. A feature map reflecting the position of a certain feature in the original image is produced by the convolution layer's filters scanning the entire input. The way that neurons in the human brain react to visual stimuli is comparable to this mechanism. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a type of artificial neural network specifically designed to process two-dimensional grid-shaped data, such as images. The convolution layer, pooling layer, and fully connected layer are the three primary hierarchical layers of a CNN. The central component of a CNN is the convolution layer, where different visual elements like edges, textures, and patterns are detected by applying filters or kernels to the input. A feature map reflecting the position of a certain feature in the original image is produced by the convolution layer's filters scanning the entire input. The way that neurons in the human brain react to visual stimuli is comparable to this mechanism. (Prediction of Ball Position Using CNN Methods With Zed Camera on Goalkeeper Robot Application, page 4)

4. The Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model is trained using the prepared dataset. CNN is a type of deep neural network that is highly effective for the analysis and processing of visual data such as images and videos. In this context, CNN is used to predict the position of the ball based on the position data that has been collected during the training session. The training process involves adjusting the weights of the model through the backpropagation technique to minimize the prediction error. The Fig. 7 is a sequential model of the CNN architecture for ball position prediction. A sequential model is a series of layers that are processed sequentially from input to output. The given model consists of several types of layers: Conv1D, AveragePooling1D, Dropout, MaxPooling1D, Flatten, and Dense. The operation process is in equations ( 4) to (9). (Prediction of Ball Position Using CNN Methods With Zed Camera on Goalkeeper Robot Application, page 7)

5. The pooling layer, which comes after the convolution layer, is meant to combine key information and lower the dimensionality of the feature map. Max pooling, which chooses the maximum value within each condensed area of the feature map, is a frequently used kind of pooling. This lessens the number of parameters that must be computed and increases the model's resistance to slight variations in the input features' locations.

CNNs typically have multiple sets of successive convolution and pooling layers, which allow the network to detect increasingly complex features at each layer. Early layers may detect simple edges and lines, while deeper layers may detect more complex objects, such as specific shapes and patterns.

The final input is supplied into the fully connected layer after passing through several convolution and pooling layers. Every neuron in this layer is connected to every other neuron in the layer before it, enabling the network to compile the features that were taken out of the earlier levels and come to a conclusion. An activation function that aids in the final classification, such as ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit) or Softmax, typically follows this completely connected layer.

This study designs and implements appropriate parameter values in each layer of the CNN used. Previous researchers have created several methods for artificial intelligence that have been tried to be implemented on the ERSOW robot. CNN can also be used for object detection and position prediction in three-dimensional environments because of its ability to extract complex visual features from image data taken from the camera. The CNN method is able to process image data in two dimensions, such as applications for detecting the position of the ball in real-time for goalkeeper robots [4], [5], [25]. The CNN method is also used for several mobile robot-vision applications [26], [27] such as service robots or collaboration of several industrial robots [28], [29]. This research aims to build a combination of ZED camera devices with CNN methods that have been used in previous research to detect and predict the position of the ball in the goal area. This model scenario is to be able to reach all lighting conditions with a camera that has artificial intelligence features. The CNN model as an intelligence feature is added so that the system can predict the position of the ball with a ZED camera that has features that can overcome changes in light intensity levels. (Prediction of Ball Position Using CNN Methods With Zed Camera on Goalkeeper Robot Application, page 1)

CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) digunakan sebagai alat pemrosesan gambar untuk mengekstrak fitur-fitur penting dalam citra. CNN digunakan sebagai komponen utama dalam sistem AI karena kemampuannya untuk mengekstrak fitur-fitur kompleks dari data visual, seperti gambar dan video. CNN dapat digunakan untuk berbagai aplikasi, termasuk deteksi posisi bola di lapangan sepak bola menggunakan kamera ZED.

Dalam konteks sistem AI, CNN bekerja sebagai lapisan pemrosesan suatu citra yang menerima input dari kamera dan menghasilkan output berupa hasil pengenalan atau klasifikasi. CNN dapat digunakan untuk menyelesaikan tugas-tugas seperti deteksi objek, pengenalan wajah, dan analisis citra medis.

Dengan demikian, CNN merupakan alat penting dalam sistem AI yang memungkinkan perangkat lunak untuk menerima input visual dan menghasilkan output yang relevan dengan informasi yang terkandung di dalamnya.

2. According to Colakoglu et al. [58], class-level metrics that have been mostly used in SFP studies are CK metrics (WMC, RFC, LCOM, CBO, DIT, NOC), MC (Method/Message Complexity), CWC (Coupling Weight for a Class), AC (Attribute Complexity), CLC (Class Complexity), AMCC (Average Method Complexity per Class), ACC (Average Class Complexity), ACF (Average Coupling Factor) and AAC (Average Attributes Per Class). However, these software metrics can only be applied in particular application domains. For instance, although Rathore and Kumar [8] suggested that object-oriented metrics, particular CK metrics, are good predictors of fault severity in software project, in [59], Bansal argued that the DIT and LCOM metrics are unsuitable to measure quality and complexity for object-oriented design; whilst NOC cannot be used at all for fault-proneness prediction. As a result, when conducting SFP studies, there is always a need to select the best combination of metrics for each different application domain for the given application context. (Error-Type—A Novel Set of Software Metrics for Software Fault Prediction, page 1)

Based on the findings of this investigation, CNN models were included in the hardware, as indicated in Table 1, although further research is needed to improve system performance (mAP, AR, F1 score) and speed up inference time. Based on previous studies on road damage, several researchers have utilized the CNN model by optimizing its network structure. 7. This chapter discusses the results of the dataset that has been created as well as the results of the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) testing that has been carried out. In this research, we produced a comprehensive dataset specifically designed for applications involving wheeled soccer goalkeeper robots. The dataset includes a variety of scenarios capturing different ball movements, speeds, shooting angles, and environmental conditions to ensure robustness and versatility.

The development, implementation, and compilation processes in this study were performed on a system with the specifications listed in Table 2. These specifications include various hardware components such as high-performance CPUs, GPUs, and adequate RAM, as well as software components including operating systems, deep learning frameworks, and data processing libraries. The choice of hardware and software was critical to achieve optimal performance, enabling efficient handling of complex algorithms and large volumes of data during the development, testing, and evaluation phases.

Using the right hardware ensured fast processing times and the ability to run intensive computations necessary for training deep learning models. Meanwhile, the selection of appropriate software provided the tools needed for data preprocessing, model training, and evaluation. For instance, the use of deep learning frameworks like TensorFlow facilitated the construction and training of the CNN model, while data processing libraries such as NumPy and Pandas were essential for managing and manipulating the dataset.

At epochs 0 to 20, training accuracy jumps significantly followed by a similar increase in validation accuracy. Table 3 presents the performance report of the proposed model, a CNN-based machine learning model, in classifying test data into three categories: ''right,'' ''left,'' and ''center.'' With 180 test samples, the model achieved an overall accuracy of 70%, indicating that 70% of its predictions were correct. Table 3 shows the result of proposed method and other comparison models. From the performance evaluation results of the CNN prediction model for ball position, it was found that the model performed well for the prediction of the ''right'' and ''left'' classes, with F1-score of 0.84 and 0.76 respectively, indicating that the model was quite reliable in classifying both classes. However, the model performance for the ''center'' class showed a significant decrease, with an F1-score of only 0.39. This suggests either an imbalance in the data or a complexity in the ball movement pattern at the center that is difficult for the model to identify.

These findings show that while the CNN model is effective for most scenarios, there are areas that require improvement, especially in predicting the ''center'' class. One of the future development plans is to improve the data distribution by rebalancing the dataset so that the ''center'' class has more training examples. In addition, more complex models will be developed using other deep learning techniques, such as integration with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to better capture temporal patterns in ball movement.

For the future, some other approaches that can be developed include the use of data augmentation to generate more variations of the ball position in the ''center'' class, as well as further tuning the CNN architecture to reduce the overfitting phenomenon detected in some epochs during training. The use of attention mechanisms can also be implemented to help the model focus on key features of the ball movement, so as to improve prediction accuracy, especially in the ''center'' class which tends to be less accurate. (Prediction of Ball Position Using CNN Methods With Zed Camera on Goalkeeper Robot Application, page 9)

8. In this study, software metrics have been imported from the BugHunter Dataset and re-validated using Metric-sReloaded [49], which is a tool for obtaining/measuring software metrics from source codes. The software metrics we used in this study are at the class level and can be found in Table 2.

The reasons we employed the BugHunter Dataset are (1) the software metrics were collected from large industrial projects which are still actively maintained; (2) the source codes of the projects are publicly available via GitHub [50] for us to verify the correctness of the collected software metrics and extract the ESM values; and (3) the BugHunter Dataset collects software metrics based on before-fix and after-fix snapshots of the source code elements that were affected by bugs whilst leaving the source code elements that were not affected by bugs untouched. This approach is useful to capture the changes in software metrics when a bug is being fixed. The empirical evaluations showed that the dataset can be used for further investigations such as bug prediction. (Error-Type—A Novel Set of Software Metrics for Software Fault Prediction, page 5)

Menurut konteks yang disediakan, software metrics dapat digunakan untuk mengevaluasi model CNN dalam beberapa cara:

Dalam eksperimen yang dilakukan, ditemukan bahwa penggunaan metrik ESM baru memberikan informasi lebih bermanfaat kepada model belajar mesin dan meningkatkan performa model.
2. **Penggunaan data processing libraries**: Data processing libraries seperti NumPy dan Pandas dapat digunakan untuk mengelola dan memanipulasi dataset yang digunakan dalam pelatihan model CNN.
3. **Penggunaan deep learning frameworks**: Deep learning frameworks seperti TensorFlow dapat digunakan untuk membangun dan melatih model CNN.

Dengan demikian, software metrics dapat membantu meningkatkan performa model CNN dan memberikan informasi lebih bermanfaat dalam proses pelatihan dan evaluasi model.

According to Colakoglu et al. [58], class-level metrics that have been mostly used in SFP studies are CK metrics (WMC, RFC, LCOM, CBO, DIT, NOC), MC (Method/Message Complexity), CWC (Coupling Weight for a Class), AC (Attribute Complexity), CLC (Class Complexity), AMCC (Average Method Complexity per Class), ACC (Average Class Complexity), ACF (Average Coupling Factor) and AAC (Average Attributes Per Class). However, these software metrics can only be applied in particular application domains. For instance, although Rathore and Kumar [8] suggested that object-oriented metrics, particular CK metrics, are good predictors of fault severity in software project, in [59], Bansal argued that the DIT and LCOM metrics are unsuitable to measure quality and complexity for object-oriented design; whilst NOC cannot be used at all for fault-proneness prediction. As a result, when conducting SFP studies, there is always a need to select the best combination of metrics for each different application domain for the given application context. (Error-Type—A Novel Set of Software Metrics for Software Fault Prediction, page 1)

2. The road damage detection research makes use of laser sensors to rebuild 3D road damage as well as stereo vision technologies. Several sensors are required for the stereo vision system, including two cameras, an LED, a laser, and LiDAR. The laser sensor has a small beamwidth; thus, it cannot detect road damage in the form of a large hole, necessitating the use of an array of LEDs, lasers, LiDARs, and other sensors [18], [49]. Reconstructing the pothole takes time, whether using an LED array, laser, or LiDAR. Furthermore, 3D road defect reconstruction and stereo vision require well-lit lighting and slow vehicle speeds [17], [18], [50].

Further research used image-processing techniques. Potholes are a form of road irregularity that can be recognized with traditional image processing techniques. To achieve high accuracy, this technique takes numerous steps, including manual image feature extraction and image processing parameter adjustments. As a result, the image frame rate varies depending on traffic circumstances [21]. Some research that investigated road conditions, pavement conditions, potholes, cracks, smart phone sensors, and accelerometers used machine learning techniques such as support vector machines, neural networks, multilayer perceptron, and decision trees [16]. Furthermore, research is being conducted to detect pavement damage using ML algorithms such as support vector machines, artificial neural networks, and random forests [51]. To improve accuracy, ML models require significant computer resources during data processing, which also includes manual feature analysis.

Several studies used deep convolutional neural network (CNN) techniques to automate the simultaneous feature extraction and categorization of objects [41], [52]. This is challenging to incorporate into real-time road defect detection systems. The deployment of CNN models for road damage detection on devices requires a balance between high accuracy and high efficiency [53]. The use of CNN models for road damage detection on devices requires achieving a balance between high accuracy and high efficiency. The use of CNN models for road damage detection on devices necessitates striking a balance between high accuracy and high efficiency. The parameter system performance deployment model CNN on devices performs well in terms of precision, recall, F1-score, and as well as efficiency of time inference.

The CNN models perform exceptionally well in terms of high accuracy, precision, recall, and low loss. This requires CNN models with large architecture and competitive computing costs that are inefficient. To do this while maintaining high accuracy, a simplified CNN model configuration setting is required to achieve good CNN model system performance. High efficiency, which is the CNN model system performance, enables it to detect road faults on edge devices with a short inference time. Because the CNN model on edge devices have limited storage capacity, inference time must be considered. Taking this into account, the CNN model offers good system performance and a short inference time for simpler model configurations, but high accuracy is difficult to achieve. To obtain optimal system performance, the CNN model parameters must be properly chosen. When selecting a detection model, there is no definitive answer as to which model has the best performance [31], [53].

Improving system performance in computer vision, object recognition, and classification using CNN models can be achieved through various methods. These include modifying or adding components to the CNN model structure and optimizing hyperparameter selection during CNN model training. The strategy of enhancing the CNN structure aims to improve feature extraction efficiency and model accuracy by modifying or incorporating new components into the CNN architecture. Several studies have focused on enhancing CNN models by modifying or adding components to the existing CNN structure [54], [55], [56], [57], [58], [59]. DenseNet was integrated into the YOLOv4 backbone to optimize feature transfer and reuse. This involved several modifications, such as adjusting the Path Aggregation Network (PANet) [54], introducing New Residual Blocks, applying Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP), modifying the PANet, and utilizing Hard-Swish activation functions [59]. Similarly, researchers have integrated DenseNet blocks into the YOLOv5 backbone to enhance the preservation and reuse of critical feature information. This was achieved by incorporating a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) [56]. Another study introduced a novel framework called Multiple Graph Learning Neural Networks (MGLNN) for semi-supervised learning on graph-based data [55]. Additionally, modifications were made to the YOLO model using the CSPDarknet53 backbone structure, which included Residual Blocks, DenseNet, Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP), and the Path Aggregation Network (PANet) [57]. (iYOLOV7-TPE-SS: Leveraging Improved YOLO Model With Multilevel Hyperparameter Optimization for Road Damage Detection on Edge Devices, page 2)

3. Typically machine learning focus on design and development of algorithms with techniques. That extricate rules, and patterns from massive databases. Neural Networks (NN) are previously being utilized within the software to create reliability growth models for the prediction of total modification or reusability metrics. The NN model is trained to do again a stipulated series of exact instances classification, as an alternative to creating formulas or rules. Mahajan et. al [38] mentioned that machine learning methods are beneficial to determine software faults as complete processing is performed by the computer. (Efficacy of Inheritance Aspect in Software Fault Prediction—A Survey Paper, page 1)

4. The Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model is trained using the prepared dataset. CNN is a type of deep neural network that is highly effective for the analysis and processing of visual data such as images and videos. In this context, CNN is used to predict the position of the ball based on the position data that has been collected during the training session. The training process involves adjusting the weights of the model through the backpropagation technique to minimize the prediction error. The Fig. 7 is a sequential model of the CNN architecture for ball position prediction. A sequential model is a series of layers that are processed sequentially from input to output. The given model consists of several types of layers: Conv1D, AveragePooling1D, Dropout, MaxPooling1D, Flatten, and Dense. The operation process is in equations ( 4) to (9). (Prediction of Ball Position Using CNN Methods With Zed Camera on Goalkeeper Robot Application, page 7)

5. Qurishee [71] presented an autonomous pavement condition evaluation employing deep learning, an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), and Raspberry Pi tiny computer technologies, which improves road maintenance and renovation management efficiency and cost effectiveness. A lowcost Raspberry Pi smart defect-detecting camera was set up with the trained SSD MobileNet v1, which can be deployed with a UAV for real-time and remote pavement condition inspection. According to preliminary data, the smart pavement detector camera achieves 60% accuracy at 1.2 frames per second on the Raspberry Pi and 96% accuracy at 13.8 frames per second on a CPU-based computer. Hassan et al. [72] employs CNN models that are improved tiny YOLO V3 on UAVs and achieves good results, with precision, sensitivity, and F1 score values better than 85%, but without considering FPS. Sathvik et al. [39] introduce

The YOLO V7 model had an F1 score of 0.51, which improved proportionally (the higher the F1 score, the more efficient the training model) as the number of epochs increased. The YOLO V7 runs on a CPU-based computer, however it does not consider run on edge devices.

Several studies using CNN models deployed on NVIDIA Jetson Nano devices include the SSD-MobileNet model with a batch size of 64 and mAP of 0.22 [48], the MobileNet V2 model, and the SSD Resnet50V1 model [34], [35]. The MobileNet V2 model using hyperparameter settings has a higher mAP of 0.0869 and average recall 0.241 than the SSD Resnet50V1. Yebes et al. [40] created a massive dataset of images with pothole annotations and road scenes from many cities across the world, captured with various cameras, vehicles, and viewpoints under varying environmental circumstances. Their fine-tuned Faster R-CNN Inception v2, Faster R-CNN Resnet101, and Faster R-CNN Inception-Resnet v2 models reached precision 75%, and their CNN model deployed the pothole detector on the Nvidia DrivePX2 platform running at 5-6 frames per second. Based on the findings of this investigation, CNN models were included in the hardware, as indicated in Table 1, although further research is needed to improve system performance (mAP, AR, F1 score) and speed up inference time. Based on previous studies on road damage, several researchers have utilized the CNN model by optimizing its network structure. Specifically, the YOLO model automates the network structure through the introduction of a new module. However, few YOLOv3 models incorporate hyperparameter optimization, with only one study utilizing the Bayesian method. (iYOLOV7-TPE-SS: Leveraging Improved YOLO Model With Multilevel Hyperparameter Optimization for Road Damage Detection on Edge Devices, page 1)

7. This chapter discusses the results of the dataset that has been created as well as the results of the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) testing that has been carried out. In this research, we produced a comprehensive dataset specifically designed for applications involving wheeled soccer goalkeeper robots. The dataset includes a variety of scenarios capturing different ball movements, speeds, shooting angles, and environmental conditions to ensure robustness and versatility.

The development, implementation, and compilation processes in this study were performed on a system with the specifications listed in Table 2. These specifications include various hardware components such as high-performance CPUs, GPUs, and adequate RAM, as well as software components including operating systems, deep learning frameworks, and data processing libraries. The choice of hardware and software was critical to achieve optimal performance, enabling efficient handling of complex algorithms and large volumes of data during the development, testing, and evaluation phases.

Using the right hardware ensured fast processing times and the ability to run intensive computations necessary for training deep learning models. Meanwhile, the selection of appropriate software provided the tools needed for data preprocessing, model training, and evaluation. For instance, the use of deep learning frameworks like TensorFlow facilitated the construction and training of the CNN model, while data processing libraries such as NumPy and Pandas were essential for managing and manipulating the dataset.

Comparisons results of the proposed system with related works. measures the model's performance on a separate dataset. A large gap between these two lines may indicate overfitting.

At epochs 0 to 20, training accuracy jumps significantly followed by a similar increase in validation accuracy. At epochs 21 to 40, there is a slight increase in training accuracy with a short period of decline before rising again, while validation accuracy rises significantly and then falls sharply before rising again. At epochs 41 to 60, both graphs show steady fluctuations. At epochs 61 to 80, the fluctuation pattern continued on both graphs. At the last epochs, 81 to 100, there is a significant drop in training accuracy followed immediately by a rapid rise, while validation accuracy shows a continuous up and down trend with no apparent stability. Testing was conducted to evaluate the performance of the trained model. Table 3 presents the performance report of the proposed model, a CNN-based machine learning model, in classifying test data into three categories: ''right,'' ''left,'' and ''center.'' With 180 test samples, the model achieved an overall accuracy of 70%, indicating that 70% of its predictions were correct. Table 3 shows the result of proposed method and other comparison models. From the performance evaluation results of the CNN prediction model for ball position, it was found that the model performed well for the prediction of the ''right'' and ''left'' classes, with F1-score of 0.84 and 0.76 respectively, indicating that the model was quite reliable in classifying both classes. However, the model performance for the ''center'' class showed a significant decrease, with an F1-score of only 0.39. This suggests either an imbalance in the data or a complexity in the ball movement pattern at the center that is difficult for the model to identify.

These findings show that while the CNN model is effective for most scenarios, there are areas that require improvement, especially in predicting the ''center'' class. One of the future development plans is to improve the data distribution by rebalancing the dataset so that the ''center'' class has more training examples. In addition, more complex models will be developed using other deep learning techniques, such as integration with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to better capture temporal patterns in ball movement.

For the future, some other approaches that can be developed include the use of data augmentation to generate more variations of the ball position in the ''center'' class, as well as further tuning the CNN architecture to reduce the overfitting phenomenon detected in some epochs during training. The use of attention mechanisms can also be implemented to help the model focus on key features of the ball movement, so as to improve prediction accuracy, especially in the ''center'' class which tends to be less accurate. (Prediction of Ball Position Using CNN Methods With Zed Camera on Goalkeeper Robot Application, page 9)

8. In pursuance of the issues raised from the empirical literature, it is necessary for process theory to transform software engineering body of knowledge especially paying attention to SSCs. Additionally, research in software engineering has been predominately prescriptive and method-focused [39], producing thousands of software development methods that remain underutilized. In order to solve the challenges with software practice, practitioners and researchers should contribute to the body of knowledge [135], given that SSCs dominate the industry and are responsible for over 80% of software produced in the market. (Software Engineering in Small Software Companies: Consolidating and Integrating Empirical Literature Into a Process Tool Adoption Framework, page 1)

### response

Software engineering dapat membantu pengembangan sistem berbasis CNN dengan beberapa cara:

1. **Mengidentifikasi dan mengatasi masalah**: Dengan menggunakan pendekatan ilmiah, software engineering dapat membantu mengidentifikasi masalah-masalah yang mungkin timbul dalam pengembangan sistem berbasis CNN, seperti kesalahan klasifikasi, overfitting, atau kekurangan data.
2. **Mengembangkan metode dan algoritma**: Software engineering dapat membantu mengembangkan metode dan algoritma baru untuk meningkatkan kinerja sistem berbasis CNN, seperti penggunaan teknik transfer learning, augmentation data, atau kombinasi model.
3. **Mengintegrasikan sistem**: Software engineering dapat membantu mengintegrasikan sistem berbasis CNN dengan sistem lainnya, seperti sistem keamanan, sistem monitoring, atau sistem otomatisasi.
4. **Meningkatkan efisiensi dan skalabilitas**: Software engineering dapat membantu meningkatkan efisiensi dan skalabilitas sistem berbasis CNN dengan menggunakan teknik optimisasi, caching data, atau penggunaan teknologi cloud computing.

Dalam konteks yang disebutkan di artikel, software engineering digunakan untuk mengembangkan sistem penambang emosi (sentiment analysis) berdasarkan CNN. Dengan menggunakan pendekatan ilmiah dan metode-metode baru, tim peneliti dapat meningkatkan kinerja sistem tersebut dan membuatnya lebih efektif dalam mendeteksi emosi pengguna.

Several studies using CNN models deployed on NVIDIA Jetson Nano devices include the SSD-MobileNet model with a batch size of 64 and mAP of 0.22 [48], the MobileNet V2 model, and the SSD Resnet50V1 model [34], [35]. The MobileNet V2 model using hyperparameter settings has a higher mAP of 0.0869 and average recall 0.241 than the SSD Resnet50V1. Yebes et al. [40] created a massive dataset of images with pothole annotations and road scenes from many cities across the world, captured with various cameras, vehicles, and viewpoints under varying environmental circumstances. Their fine-tuned Faster R-CNN Inception v2, Faster R-CNN Resnet101, and Faster R-CNN Inception-Resnet v2 models reached precision 75%, and their CNN model deployed the pothole detector on the Nvidia DrivePX2 platform running at 5-6 frames per second. Based on the findings of this investigation, CNN models were included in the hardware, as indicated in Table 1, although further research is needed to improve system performance (mAP, AR, F1 score) and speed up inference time. Based on previous studies on road damage, several researchers have utilized the CNN model by optimizing its network structure. Specifically, the YOLO model automates the network structure through the introduction of a new module. However, few YOLOv3 models incorporate hyperparameter optimization, with only one study utilizing the Bayesian method. (iYOLOV7-TPE-SS: Leveraging Improved YOLO Model With Multilevel Hyperparameter Optimization for Road Damage Detection on Edge Devices, page 1)

(Prediction of Ball Position Using CNN Methods With Zed Camera on Goalkeeper Robot Application, page 10)

This chapter discusses the results of the dataset that has been created as well as the results of the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) testing that has been carried out. In this research, we produced a comprehensive dataset specifically designed for applications involving wheeled soccer goalkeeper robots. The dataset includes a variety of scenarios capturing different ball movements, speeds, shooting angles, and environmental conditions to ensure robustness and versatility. The development, implementation, and compilation processes in this study were performed on a system with the specifications listed in Table 2. These specifications include various hardware components such as high-performance CPUs, GPUs, and adequate RAM, as well as software components including operating systems, deep learning frameworks, and data processing libraries. The choice of hardware and software was critical to achieve optimal performance, enabling efficient handling of complex algorithms and large volumes of data during the development, testing, and evaluation phases. Using the right hardware ensured fast processing times and the ability to run intensive computations necessary for training deep learning models. Meanwhile, the selection of appropriate software provided the tools needed for data preprocessing, model training, and evaluation. For instance, the use of deep learning frameworks like TensorFlow facilitated the construction and training of the CNN model, while data processing libraries such as NumPy and Pandas were essential for managing and manipulating the dataset. TABLE 2. Computer specification. The model's overall accuracy is approximately 98.02%, calculated as follows by equations ( 11) to (14). Precision, measuring the proportion of correct ball predictions out of all ball predictions, is very high at 99.75%: Recall, or sensitivity, measuring the proportion of correctly identified balls out of all actual balls, is also high at 98.26%: The F1 Score, the harmonic mean of precision and recall, is around 99.00%: These metrics indicate that the model has high performance in detecting balls, although it struggles with correctly identifying the background. TABLE 3. Comparisons results of the proposed system with related works. measures the model's performance on a separate dataset. A large gap between these two lines may indicate overfitting. At epochs 0 to 20, training accuracy jumps significantly followed by a similar increase in validation accuracy. At epochs 21 to 40, there is a slight increase in training accuracy with a short period of decline before rising again, while validation accuracy rises significantly and then falls sharply before rising again. At epochs 41 to 60, both graphs show steady fluctuations. At epochs 61 to 80, the fluctuation pattern continued on both graphs. At the last epochs, 81 to 100, there is a significant drop in training accuracy followed immediately by a rapid rise, while validation accuracy shows a continuous up and down trend with no apparent stability. Testing was conducted to evaluate the performance of the trained model. Table 3 presents the performance report of the proposed model, a CNN-based machine learning model, in classifying test data into three categories: ''right,'' ''left,'' and ''center.'' With 180 test samples, the model achieved an overall accuracy of 70%, indicating that 70% of its predictions were correct. Table 3 shows the result of proposed method and other comparison models. From the performance evaluation results of the CNN prediction model for ball position, it was found that the model performed well for the prediction of the ''right'' and ''left'' classes, with F1-score of 0.84 and 0.76 respectively, indicating that the model was quite reliable in classifying both classes. However, the model performance for the ''center'' class showed a significant decrease, with an F1-score of only 0.39. This suggests either an imbalance in the data or a complexity in the ball movement pattern at the center that is difficult for the model to identify. These findings show that while the CNN model is effective for most scenarios, there are areas that require improvement, especially in predicting the ''center'' class. One of the future development plans is to improve the data distribution by rebalancing the dataset so that the ''center'' class has more training examples. In addition, more complex models will be developed using other deep learning techniques, such as integration with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to better capture temporal patterns in ball movement. For the future, some other approaches that can be developed include the use of data augmentation to generate more variations of the ball position in the ''center'' class, as well as further tuning the CNN architecture to reduce the overfitting phenomenon detected in some epochs during training. The use of attention mechanisms can also be implemented to help the model focus on key features of the ball movement, so as to improve prediction accuracy, especially in the ''center'' class which tends to be less accurate. (Prediction of Ball Position Using CNN Methods With Zed Camera on Goalkeeper Robot Application, page 9)

In pursuance of the issues raised from the empirical literature, it is necessary for process theory to transform software engineering body of knowledge especially paying attention to SSCs. Additionally, research in software engineering has been predominately prescriptive and method-focused [39], producing thousands of software development methods that remain underutilized. In order to solve the challenges with software practice, practitioners and researchers should contribute to the body of knowledge [135], given that SSCs dominate the industry and are responsible for over 80% of software produced in the market. (Software Engineering in Small Software Companies: Consolidating and Integrating Empirical Literature Into a Process Tool Adoption Framework, page 1)
